operations.specification: Guest user registration operation that creates a temporary guest account with minimal required information. The operation associates a guest user with a session token and refresh token for accessing public article browsing and comment viewing features. This operation is part of the discussion_board_guest authentication system and does not require email verification or complex authentication setup.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new guest user account for temporary access to the discussion board.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows unauthenticated visitors to create a temporary guest account for browsing published articles and reading comments on the discussion board without requiring email verification or user credentials.

Guest registration is a simplified onboarding process that creates a temporary user session. Unlike contributor or moderator accounts, guest accounts do not require email addresses, passwords, or account verification. The system issues both an access token and a refresh token to enable stateless API authentication while maintaining guest session management.

Guest users created through this endpoint can access only public resources: published articles and their associated comments. They cannot create articles, post comments, upload files, or perform any moderation actions. The guest account exists temporarily for the session duration and may be cleaned up after extended inactivity based on system_configurations timeout settings.

The system_configurations table controls password and session behavior, though guest accounts bypass password requirements entirely. Session timeout is configurable through the 'session_timeout_minutes' setting, and guests receive refresh tokens that must be renewed before token expiration.

This operation is public and requires no authentication. Each guest registration creates a fresh, isolated session without requiring any personal information or account recovery mechanisms. The response includes both an access token (short-lived, typically 15-60 minutes) and a refresh token (longer-lived, used to obtain new access tokens without re-registering).

Related operations include the guest token refresh endpoint (/auth/guest/refresh) which renews expired access tokens using the refresh token.

requestBody.description: Guest registration request with optional device identifier for session tracking.

responseBody.description: Guest account creation response with authentication tokens.

operations.specification: Guest user token refresh operation that renews an expired or expiring access token using a valid refresh token. This operation extends the guest session without requiring re-registration, enabling continuous browsing of the discussion board across multiple API requests.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Renew guest user access tokens using a valid refresh token.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows guest users to obtain new access tokens by presenting a valid refresh token, extending their session without requiring re-registration.

Guest users receive both short-lived access tokens and longer-lived refresh tokens upon registration. As the access token approaches expiration, guest clients should call this endpoint with their refresh token to obtain a new access token. This enables seamless, continuous access to the discussion board without interrupting the browsing experience.

The refresh operation validates that the provided refresh token is still valid (not expired, not revoked). The system_configurations table defines session timeout policies that govern how long refresh tokens remain valid. Upon successful validation, the operation returns a new access token with a fresh expiration time.

Guest refresh tokens have longer expiration periods than access tokens, typically spanning hours or days depending on system_configurations. This prevents guests from being logged out during extended browsing sessions. However, refresh tokens do eventually expire, at which point guests must re-register through the /auth/guest/join endpoint.

This operation requires a valid refresh token in the request and does not require email, password, or any credentials beyond the refresh token itself. The operation is idempotent: calling it multiple times with the same refresh token produces the same result.

Error scenarios include expired refresh tokens (guest must re-register), revoked refresh tokens (guest session terminated), or malformed token formats. The system maintains audit logs of token refresh operations for security and compliance purposes.

requestBody.description: Guest token refresh request with the refresh token.

responseBody.description: Token refresh response with new access token and updated refresh token.

operations.specification: Contributor account registration endpoint for the discussion board. Creates a new contributor account with email verification requirement and returns initial JWT tokens (access and refresh). Associated with discussion_board_contributors Prisma table.
operations.name: join
operations.summary: Register a new contributor account for the discussion board
operations.description:
Creates a new contributor account in the discussion board system. This operation registers a contributor with email, username, and password credentials stored securely with bcrypt hashing (minimum 12 salt rounds). The email address must be unique across all contributors and is required for verification before account can post articles or comments.

The contributor's password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. The username must be unique, 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only, and is immutable after creation. Upon successful registration, the account is created with 'active' account_status and email_verified set to false until the contributor clicks the verification email link.

The operation creates the initial contributor record in the discussion_board_contributors table with created_at and updated_at timestamps. The email_verified field is set to false, preventing article creation or commenting until verification is completed. Passwords are never stored plaintext but always hashed with bcrypt before database storage.

This operation returns JWT tokens (access token valid for 30 minutes, refresh token valid for 7 days) upon successful registration. A welcome email is sent to the provided email address with a verification link that contributor must click to enable full account functionality. The response includes the IDiscussionBoardContributor.IAuthorized structure with token information.

Related operations: After registration, the contributor should call the login operation to authenticate with existing credentials, or use the refresh operation to obtain new tokens using a valid refresh token.

requestBody.description: Contributor registration credentials and profile information

responseBody.description: Newly created contributor account with JWT tokens for authentication

operations.specification: Contributor account authentication endpoint for the discussion board. Validates email/username and password credentials against stored bcrypt hash and returns JWT tokens upon successful authentication. Associated with discussion_board_contributors and discussion_board_contributor_sessions Prisma tables.
operations.name: login
operations.summary: Authenticate a contributor account and obtain JWT tokens
operations.description:
Authenticates a registered contributor using email (or username) and password credentials. This operation validates that the contributor account exists in the discussion_board_contributors table, verifies the password against the stored bcrypt hash, and confirms that the account is in 'active' status and email has been verified.

The operation checks the account_status field to ensure it is 'active', rejecting authentication for accounts marked as 'suspended', 'restricted', or 'deleted'. Email verification must be complete (email_verified = true) before login is allowed. Password verification uses bcrypt comparison with the stored password_hash to prevent plaintext password exposure.

Upon successful authentication, the operation creates a new session record in the discussion_board_contributor_sessions table with connection metadata: IP address, referrer URL, and accessed URL (href). The last_login_at timestamp is updated in the contributor record. JWT tokens are issued with standard expiration (access token 30 minutes, refresh token 7 days).

The operation supports multiple concurrent sessions - one contributor can authenticate from different devices or browsers simultaneously, with each session tracked independently. Session data includes ip, href, and referrer fields for security monitoring and abuse detection.

Failed authentication attempts (invalid password, account not found, unverified email, inactive account) return appropriate error responses without exposing specific failure reasons. The response includes the IDiscussionBoardContributor.IAuthorized structure with access and refresh tokens.

Related operations: After login, contributors can use the refresh operation to obtain new tokens before expiration. Contributors who forgot their password should use the password reset flow (if available).

requestBody.description: Contributor authentication credentials for login

responseBody.description: Authenticated contributor account with JWT tokens for access

operations.specification: Token refresh endpoint for contributor sessions. Accepts a valid refresh token and returns new access and refresh tokens. Associated with discussion_board_contributor_sessions Prisma table for session validation.
operations.name: refresh
operations.summary: Refresh contributor JWT tokens using a valid refresh token
operations.description:
Renews JWT tokens for an authenticated contributor using a valid refresh token. This operation validates the provided refresh token against the contributor's session records in the discussion_board_contributor_sessions table and issues new access and refresh tokens with extended expiration.

The operation verifies that the refresh token is still valid (not expired - refresh tokens expire after 7 days) and that the associated contributor session exists and has not been explicitly terminated (expired_at is null). The session record maintains connection context (ip, href, referrer) that was created during initial login.

Upon successful token refresh, new JWT tokens are issued: an access token valid for 30 minutes for API access, and a new refresh token valid for 7 days for future token renewals. The existing session record is maintained without modification. If the refresh token has expired (7 days from session creation), the operation rejects the request and contributor must re-authenticate using the login operation.

This operation is called automatically by clients when access token approaches expiration (typically at 25-minute mark to avoid token expiration during API requests). Multiple token refreshes can occur during a session's 7-day lifetime, each issuing new tokens with fresh expiration times.

The operation validates that the associated contributor account still exists in discussion_board_contributors table and maintains 'active' account status. If account status has changed to 'suspended', 'restricted', or 'deleted' since the session was created, token refresh is denied and contributor must re-authenticate.

Failed refresh attempts (invalid token, expired token, terminated session, inactive account) return appropriate error responses. The response includes the IDiscussionBoardContributor.IAuthorized structure with new access and refresh tokens.

Related operations: This operation works in conjunction with login to maintain continuous authenticated access throughout a 7-day session window without requiring contributors to re-enter credentials.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new JWT tokens

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens with extended expiration for continued authenticated access

Email verification is required before moderators can access moderation tools.

operations.summary: Register a new moderator account for the discussion board.
operations.description:
Creates a new moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table. This endpoint accepts email, password, and username to establish a new moderator identity with administrative permissions for content moderation and user management.

The operation stores a bcrypt-hashed password with minimum 12 salt rounds and enforces password complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character). Email address must be unique across all moderator accounts and follows valid email format (user@domain.com). Username must be unique, 3-50 characters, and contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores.

The newly created moderator account is assigned 'full' moderation tier (all moderation permissions) and initialized with account_status as 'active'. However, email_verified is set to false initially, and the moderator cannot access moderation tools until verifying their email address through a confirmation link.

The operation triggers account creation timestamp (created_at) and last_login_at is set to null until first login. This endpoint is public and requires no prior authentication, allowing new moderators to self-register within the system.

Related authentication operations include POST /auth/moderator/login for existing moderators to authenticate, and POST /auth/moderator/refresh for token renewal using a valid refresh token. Account verification requires the moderator to complete email verification before gaining full moderation access.

operations.summary: Authenticate a moderator and issue JWT tokens for moderation access.
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing moderator using email and password credentials against the discussion_board_moderators table. This endpoint validates the provided email address, verifies the bcrypt-hashed password, and returns JWT access and refresh tokens upon successful authentication.

The operation validates that the email exists in the moderators table and matches the bcrypt-hashed password_hash field. All moderator passwords are hashed with minimum 12 salt rounds and must meet complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character).

Authentication requires the moderator's email_verified status to be true - moderators cannot access moderation tools until they complete email verification. If email verification is pending, the login attempt is rejected. The operation also checks account_status field and rejects login attempts for suspended or deleted moderator accounts.

Upon successful authentication, the operation updates the last_login_at timestamp to record the login time. JWT tokens are issued with appropriate expiration times: access tokens for short-term authenticated access and refresh tokens for obtaining new access tokens without re-authenticating.

This endpoint is public and requires no prior authentication. Failed authentication attempts should return appropriate error responses without revealing whether the email exists (security best practice). Related operations include POST /auth/moderator/join for new moderator registration and POST /auth/moderator/refresh for token renewal.

operations.description:
Refreshes the JWT access token for an authenticated moderator using a valid refresh token. This operation accepts a refresh token issued during login or registration and validates it against the moderator's active session in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. Upon validation, a new access token is issued for continued authenticated access to moderation features.

The operation validates that the provided refresh token is valid, has not expired, and belongs to an existing moderator account. The refresh token is validated against the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table which maintains session state for authenticated moderators. If the token is invalid, expired, or the associated moderator account has been suspended or deleted, the refresh attempt is rejected.

The operation also checks that the moderator's account_status field is 'active' and email_verified is true - if either condition fails, token refresh is rejected to prevent access by suspended or unverified accounts. The refreshed access token is issued with a new expiration time, allowing continuous authenticated access without requiring the moderator to re-enter their password.

This endpoint requires a valid refresh token but does not require the moderator to be currently authenticated with an access token. The refresh token serves as proof of prior successful authentication. New refresh tokens may or may not be issued depending on implementation (typically refresh tokens remain valid across multiple refresh operations until they expire).

Related authentication operations include POST /auth/moderator/join for new moderator registration and POST /auth/moderator/login for credential-based authentication.

operations.specification: This operation initiates a password reset request for a contributor account. It accepts an email address and generates a secure, time-limited password reset token that is sent to the contributor's registered email address. The reset token is valid for 30 minutes and can only be used once. This operation corresponds to the discussion_board_contributors table and implements account recovery functionality that allows contributors to regain access to their accounts if they forget their passwords.
operations.summary: Request a password reset token for a contributor account via email
operations.description:
Initiate a password reset request by providing the email address associated with a contributor account. This operation validates that the email address exists in the system and generates a secure, time-limited token for password recovery.

The password reset token is sent via email to the registered address and is valid for exactly 30 minutes from generation. The token is single-use and becomes invalid after one successful password reset or after the 30-minute expiration window closes. If a contributor requests multiple resets, only the most recent token remains valid.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent brute-force enumeration attacks on email addresses. The operation does not reveal whether an email address is registered in the system (returns success regardless) to prevent account enumeration. Failed password resets due to expired or invalid tokens should not expose token validity information.

This operation works in conjunction with the reset-password endpoint, which must be called with the token and new password to complete the account recovery process. Contributors with suspended or deleted accounts cannot request password resets, and the system returns generic responses for these cases to avoid leaking account status information.

requestBody.description: Email address of the contributor account for which password reset is requested

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: This operation completes the password reset process by accepting a valid reset token and a new password. It validates the token's authenticity, checks that it has not expired (within 30 minutes of generation), and that it has not been previously used. Upon successful validation, the new password is hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds and replaces the old password. The password_changed_at timestamp is updated to the current time, and all existing sessions for the contributor are invalidated. This operation corresponds to the discussion_board_contributors table and implements the second step of the password recovery workflow.
operations.summary: Reset a contributor account password using a valid reset token
operations.description:
Complete the password reset process by submitting a valid reset token and a new password. This operation validates the token and implements the new password with strict security requirements.

The reset token must have been generated by the request-password-reset endpoint and must not have expired (valid for 30 minutes from generation). If the token has been used previously or its validity period has elapsed, the operation rejects the request. Each token can only be used once; subsequent attempts with the same token are rejected.

The new password must meet all security requirements: minimum 8 characters in length, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character. Password strength validation occurs before the password is hashed. Passwords cannot match the contributor's previous password to prevent reuse of recently compromised credentials.

Password hashing is performed using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds, ensuring cryptographically secure storage that cannot be reversed even if the database is compromised. Upon successful password change, the password_changed_at field is updated to reflect the modification timestamp. Critically, all existing sessions for the contributor are immediately invalidated, forcing re-authentication on all devices and sessions.

Security considerations include preventing timing attacks by using consistent response times regardless of token validity. The operation does not reveal whether a token is invalid due to expiration, previous use, or incorrect format, to prevent token validation enumeration attacks. Only valid reset operations update account timestamps, minimizing information disclosure.

Fetch the current authenticated user's profile including account details, email, username, account status, and verification state.

This operation returns the authenticated user's complete profile information from either the discussion_board_contributors or discussion_board_moderators table depending on their user type. The response includes email address, username, account status (active, suspended, restricted, or deleted), email verification state, and timestamp information for account creation and last login.

For contributors, the response includes contributor-specific metadata such as last login timestamp and password change timestamp. For moderators, the response includes moderation tier information and last access to the moderation dashboard.

Security considerations: This operation requires authentication via JWT token. The endpoint only returns profile information for the authenticated user; cross-user profile access is not permitted. Sensitive information such as password hash is never included in the response. The operation respects the user's account status (suspended accounts can still view their own profile) and returns current data reflecting any recent moderator actions or account changes.

Related operations: The PUT /profile endpoint allows users to update their own profile information such as email or username. Account creation and authentication are handled through separate authentication service endpoints (not managed by this API).

The operation maintains audit trail compatibility by recording access timestamps in last_login_at (contributors) or updated profile state queries.

The endpoint supports updates to user account details such as email address and username for both contributors and moderators. operations.summary: Update the authenticated user's profile information
operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile information such as email address and username.

This operation allows authenticated users (contributors and moderators) to modify their own account information. The operation accepts updates to fields such as email address and username while enforcing uniqueness constraints and format validation rules. Email must be in valid format (user@domain.com) and unique across all accounts of the same user type. Username must be 3-50 characters, alphanumeric with underscores, and unique across accounts of the same user type.

The operation updates the appropriate table (discussion_board_contributors or discussion_board_moderators) based on the authenticated user's type. The updated_at timestamp is automatically recorded to reflect the modification time. All updates are applied atomically; if any validation fails, no changes are persisted.

Security considerations: This operation requires authentication via JWT token. Users can only update their own profile; cross-user profile modifications are not permitted. Certain fields such as account_status, password (managed through separate password change endpoint), and moderation_tier (for moderators) cannot be modified through this operation. Password changes are handled through a dedicated password management endpoint that requires additional verification. Account status changes can only be performed by moderators through administrative operations.

Validation rules: Email addresses must follow RFC 5321 standards. Usernames must match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{3,50}$. Duplicate email or username values across the user's account type will result in HTTP 409 Conflict error with descriptive message indicating which field caused the conflict.

Related operations: GET /profile retrieves current profile information. Separate password change endpoint handles password updates with additional security requirements. Account status changes and other administrative modifications are performed by moderators through moderation endpoints.

The operation returns the complete updated profile information confirming all modifications were successfully applied.

It operates on the discussion_board_contributors table and implements soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time. The contributor's account status is changed to 'deleted', marking the account for deletion while preserving all data for audit and recovery purposes. Soft-deleted accounts are retained for 6 months to enable recovery; after 6 months, the account and associated data can be permanently purged. The operation requires password verification to prevent accidental or unauthorized account deletion.
operations.summary: Soft-delete contributor account
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authenticated contributors to delete their own account through a soft-delete operation. The account is marked for deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time and changing the account_status to 'deleted', while all data is retained in the database for audit trail and recovery purposes.

The discussion_board_contributors table uses soft deletion to preserve contributor information and maintain data integrity for associated articles and comments. Deleted accounts are retained for 6 months to enable recovery through administrator support; after 6 months, the account and related data can be permanently purged from the system.

Security and authorization require password verification before account deletion to prevent unauthorized or accidental deletion. The operation disables all active sessions for the contributor, preventing further access immediately after deletion.

Upon successful deletion, the contributor can no longer log in, create articles, post comments, or access any features. Articles and comments created by the deleted account remain visible in the system but are associated with a deleted contributor account. Related operations include password change (POST /profile/change-password) and account recovery (if implemented).

requestBody.description: Password verification for account deletion confirmation

responseBody.description: Confirmation message indicating successful account deletion

It operates on the discussion_board_contributors table from the Prisma schema and returns comprehensive contributor account data including email, username, account status, and authentication metadata. operations.summary: Retrieve a specific discussion board contributor's detailed account information
operations.description:
Fetch complete information about a discussion board contributor account by their unique identifier. This operation returns all relevant contributor metadata including email address, username, account status, email verification state, creation and modification timestamps, and last login information.

The contributor entity represents registered user accounts capable of creating articles and posting comments on the discussion board. Each contributor maintains unique email and username fields enforced at the database level. Account status can be 'active' for normal operations, 'suspended' for temporary bans, 'restricted' for limited posting permissions, or 'deleted' for accounts marked for soft deletion.

Security and access control are important considerations. The operation validates the contributor ID exists and is accessible. Email addresses and authentication-related timestamps should be treated as sensitive information requiring appropriate authorization checks. This operation complements list retrieval operations (PATCH /articles) and other contributor-related endpoints.

The response includes timestamp information for account creation, last modification, last successful login, and password changes. The deleted_at field indicates soft deletion status; accounts are retained for 6 months after deletion to enable recovery before permanent purge. Email verification status determines whether the account can perform authenticated actions like posting articles or comments.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered list of discussion board articles with advanced search, sorting, and filtering capabilities. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table from the Prisma schema and supports complex queries for discovering articles based on status, category, author, publication dates, and text search across title and content fields. The operation returns articles with summary information optimized for list display, including view counts, comment counts, and pinned status.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated collection of discussion board articles with comprehensive search and filtering capabilities. This operation provides advanced discovery features for finding articles based on publication status, category assignment, author, creation/publication dates, pinned status, and full-text search across article titles and content.

The article entity represents core discussion content in the platform. Articles progress through a defined lifecycle: draft (author composition) → pending_approval (moderator review) → published (publicly visible) → archived or deleted (removed from active listings). Only published articles are publicly visible by default, though filtering options allow access to other statuses based on authorization levels.

The operation supports multiple filtering dimensions: status filtering (published, draft, pending_approval, rejected, archived, deleted), category filtering for topic organization, author filtering to find contributions by specific contributors, date range filtering for discovery by creation or publication time, and full-text search capabilities across title and content fields. Sorting options include creation date, publication date, view count, comment count, and pinned status.

Pagination is implemented with configurable page sizes and offsets to handle large article collections efficiently. The response includes summary-level information optimized for listing displays, including cached comment counts for performance, view counts for popularity metrics, pinned status for featured article highlighting, and locked status for editorial control. Related operations include detailed article retrieval (GET /articles/{articleId}) and article creation/modification endpoints.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, pagination parameters, and sorting preferences for article discovery

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of article summaries matching search and filter criteria

operations.specification: This operation creates a new article in the discussion board system, allowing authenticated contributors to submit economic and political discussion content. The operation accepts article title, content, category selection, and optional attachments. Upon creation, the article is initialized in 'draft' status, allowing the contributor to save their work and return later to continue editing. The operation operates on the discussion_board_articles table and associates the article with the authenticated contributor through the discussion_board_contributor_id foreign key. Articles must meet validation requirements: title 5-200 characters, content 50-50,000 characters, and category must be one of the predefined values from article_categories table. Attachments are optional (0-10 files) with file size limits enforced during upload.
operations.summary: Create a new article draft in the discussion board
operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article in draft status. This operation allows authenticated contributors to compose articles on economic and political topics before submitting them for moderator review.

The article is initialized with 'draft' status, allowing the contributor to save their work, close the browser, and return later to continue editing without requiring moderator approval at this stage. The system automatically records the contributor's ID as the article author and sets the creation timestamp. All article content and metadata are stored in the discussion_board_articles table with references to the author contributor and selected category.

Validation is enforced for all required fields: title must be 5-200 characters describing the article topic, content must be 50-50,000 characters containing the main discussion or analysis, and category must be selected from the predefined article categories (Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation, International, Analysis, Opinion, Other Discussion). Invalid category selections are rejected with an error listing valid options.

The operation supports optional attachment uploads (images and documents) up to a maximum of 10 files per article. Attachments are validated for file type (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP for images; PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX for documents) and size limits (10MB for images, 25MB for documents) during the creation request. Multiple attachments can be provided in a single request.

Security: Only authenticated contributors can access this endpoint. The operation requires valid JWT token authentication and the contributor's account must be in 'active' status with verified email address. The system automatically associates the created article with the authenticated user's contributor ID, preventing contributors from creating articles on behalf of others. The operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized if authentication is missing or invalid, and HTTP 403 Forbidden if the contributor account is not active or email is unverified.

Related operations: After creating an article in draft status, the contributor uses PUT /articles/{articleId} to edit the article content before submission. Once ready for moderation review, the contributor calls PATCH /articles/{articleId}/submit to transition from draft to pending_approval status. GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves the full article details including metadata and attachments.

requestBody.description: Article creation payload including title, content, category, optional description, and attachment uploads

responseBody.description: Created article object with full details including ID, author info, timestamps, and attachment metadata

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the complete details of a single article from the discussion board, identified by its unique article ID. The operation operates on the discussion_board_articles table and implements visibility controls based on article status and user role. Published articles are visible to all users (guests, contributors, and moderators), while draft, pending_approval, and rejected articles are only visible to their authors and moderators. The response includes article metadata (title, content, status, author, timestamps), complete attachment list with file metadata (original filename, file size, upload timestamp, display URL), and counts of views and comments. The operation enforces soft delete visibility - articles with deleted_at timestamp are not accessible to regular users.
operations.summary: Retrieve a complete article with all details and attachments
operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a specific article from the discussion board, including content, metadata, all attachments, and related information. This operation implements comprehensive visibility controls ensuring users can only access articles they have permission to view.

Published articles (status='published') are visible to all users: guests (unauthenticated), contributors, and moderators. Draft, pending_approval, and rejected articles are restricted to their original authors and moderators only. Attempting to access a non-published article without authorization returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with message 'You do not have permission to view this article.' Deleted articles (with deleted_at timestamp) are not accessible to regular users; only moderators can view deleted articles for audit trail purposes.

The response includes complete article information: title, content body, current status (draft/pending_approval/published/rejected/archived/deleted), author name and ID, creation and modification timestamps, published_at timestamp (null if not yet published), approval information (approver moderator ID and approval notes if approved), and rejection information (rejection reason if rejected). View count and comment count are included to help users identify popular discussions.

Attachment metadata is returned for all files associated with the article, including original filename, file type, file size in bytes, MIME type for proper browser rendering, upload timestamp, uploader contributor ID, and display URL for accessing the file. Attachments are ordered by upload sequence (first uploaded appears first in the list). For articles in draft status, only the author and moderators can view attachment information. For published articles, attachment information is visible to all users.

Moderation metadata is included for moderators viewing articles: is_pinned flag (whether article is featured), is_locked flag (whether new comments are blocked), last_edited_by contributor ID if article has been edited after creation. Moderators also see the complete audit trail of modifications and approval history.

Security: Public read access is available for published articles - no authentication required. Non-published articles require authentication and ownership or moderator privileges. The operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized if a non-published article is requested without authentication. HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned if the authenticated user is not the author and not a moderator. HTTP 404 Not Found is returned if the article ID does not exist or has been permanently deleted (not soft-deleted).

Performance: Article data including content and attachments are optimized for single-article retrieval with database queries leveraging indexes on article ID and foreign key relationships. Related operations: PATCH /articles searches and lists articles with filtering and pagination. PUT /articles/{articleId} edits article content if permitted. DELETE /articles/{articleId} removes articles if permitted. GET /articles/{articleId}/comments retrieves comments on the article.

responseBody.description: Complete article details including content, metadata, status, attachments, and moderator information

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and allows authenticated contributors to modify their own articles. operations.summary: Update an article with revised content or metadata
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article by providing new content, title, category assignment, or status change. This operation allows contributors to revise their own articles in draft or rejected states.

Contributor-specific permissions apply: contributors can only modify their own unpublished articles. Article status transitions follow the defined workflow:
- Draft articles: Contributor can update content/title freely and transition to pending_approval
- Rejected articles: Contributor can update content and resubmit for approval

The operation automatically updates the modified timestamp (updated_at) and records the user who performed the edit (last_edited_by_contributor_id). The operation validates the article belongs to the authenticated contributor before allowing modifications.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching articles by status or category, POST /articles to create new articles, GET /articles/{articleId} to retrieve article details before updating, and DELETE endpoints for article removal.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the discussion board article to be updated. Must reference an existing article owned by the authenticated contributor.

responseBody.description: Complete updated discussion board article with all fields including status, metadata, and audit timestamps reflecting the modification.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing discussion board article's administrative metadata and status. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and permits moderators to update article status, approval notes, and moderation flags on any article. The operation validates that the article exists and applies moderator-level authorization checks.
operations.summary: Update article status and moderation metadata as moderator
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article's status, approval notes, pins, and locks as a moderator. This operation allows moderators to approve or reject articles, add approval feedback, pin articles for featured display, lock articles from further comments, or archive articles.

Moderator-specific permissions apply: only moderators can execute this operation and can update any article regardless of authorship. Article status transitions follow moderation workflow:
- Pending approval: Moderator can approve (→published) or reject (→rejected)
- Published articles: Moderator can update pins/locks and transition to archived
- Rejected articles: Moderator can delete
- Archived articles: Moderator can restore or delete

The operation automatically updates the modified timestamp (updated_at) and records the moderator user ID. When moderators approve articles, the published_at timestamp is set and the article becomes publicly visible. Moderators can add approval_notes (max 1,000 characters) or rejection_reason (max 500 characters) to provide feedback to contributors.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching articles by status or category, GET /articles/{articleId} to retrieve article details before moderating.

parameters.name: articleId

requestBody.description: Moderator update data including status transitions, approval/rejection notes, pin flags, and lock flags. Approval notes max 1,000 characters, Rejection reason max 500 characters.

responseBody.description: Complete updated discussion board article reflecting moderator actions including status, approval metadata, and administrative flags.

operations.summary: Delete an article (contributor)
operations.description:
Remove a discussion board article from the system as a contributor by either soft deletion (preserving record for compliance) or permanent deletion (erase all data). Soft deletion sets the deleted_at timestamp, removing public visibility while maintaining audit trail and historical records for compliance purposes. Hard deletion completely removes the article record and associated data from the database.

Contributor-specific authorization applies: contributors can only delete their own articles. Articles in draft status can be deleted by contributors at any time. Published or archived articles can only be deleted by moderators (use moderator delete endpoint). The operation validates article ownership before processing.

Cascade behavior when article is deleted:
- All comments on the article are deleted (using same soft or hard delete strategy)
- All article attachment records are removed from storage
- View counts and statistics are cleared

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} to verify article existence, PATCH /articles to list articles (which excludes deleted articles in default view), and PUT /articles/{articleId} to update article status before deletion.

Articles cannot be recovered after hard deletion, so users should confirm deletion intent before executing this operation.

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and permits moderators to remove any article. The operation handles cascade deletion of associated comments and attachments when performing hard deletion, or marks the article as deleted using soft deletion for compliance and audit trail preservation.
operations.summary: Delete an article (moderator)
operations.description:
Remove a discussion board article from the system as a moderator using soft deletion (preserving record for compliance) or permanent deletion (erase all data). Only moderators can execute this operation. Moderators can delete any article regardless of authorship or status.

Soft deletion sets the deleted_at timestamp, removing public visibility while maintaining audit trail and historical records for compliance and regulatory purposes. Hard deletion completely removes the article record and associated data from the database.

Cascade behavior when article is deleted:
- All comments on the article are deleted (using same soft or hard delete strategy)
- All article attachment records are removed from storage
- Moderation history is preserved in audit trail for compliance
- View counts and statistics are cleared

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} to verify article state, PATCH /articles to list articles (which excludes deleted articles in default view).

Articles cannot be recovered after hard deletion. Moderators should document deletion rationale in system logs.

operations.specification: This operation allows moderators to approve a pending article for publication. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, transitioning the article from pending_approval status to published status. The moderator can provide optional approval notes that are stored alongside the approval decision. The operation automatically records the moderator who performed the approval, sets the published_at timestamp, and creates an immutable audit trail entry in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for compliance tracking. Article identifiers are UUID format matching the primary key in discussion_board_articles. Only users with moderator permissions can execute this operation.
operations.summary: Approve a pending article for publication with optional moderator notes
operations.description:
Approve a discussion board article that is currently in pending_approval status, transitioning it to published status for public visibility. Moderators use this operation after reviewing article content for compliance with community guidelines. Optional approval notes (maximum 1,000 characters) can be included to provide feedback to the contributor about why the article was approved or suggestions for future contributions.

The operation updates the article's status to 'published', records the moderator performing the approval via the approved_by_moderator_id field, and sets the published_at timestamp to the current time. An immutable audit trail entry is automatically created in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table with action_type 'approved' and the approval notes, providing permanent compliance documentation.

Security context: Only authenticated moderators can invoke this operation. The moderator's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and recorded in the article's approved_by_moderator_id field. Articles must be in pending_approval status to be approved; attempting to approve articles in other statuses will result in validation errors.

Related operations: Before approving, moderators typically retrieve pending articles using the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles with status filter). The rejection endpoint (POST /articles/{articleId}/reject) is used if the moderator decides the article does not meet community standards.

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, transitioning the article from pending_approval status to rejected status. The moderator must provide a rejection reason (required, maximum 500 characters) explaining why the article does not meet community standards. The operation automatically records the moderator who performed the rejection and creates an immutable audit trail entry in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for compliance tracking. Article identifiers are UUID format matching the primary key in discussion_board_articles. Only users with moderator permissions can execute this operation.
operations.summary: Reject a pending article with required moderator feedback
operations.description:
Reject a discussion board article that is currently in pending_approval status, transitioning it to rejected status and preventing publication. Moderators use this operation after reviewing article content and determining it does not meet community guidelines or quality standards. A rejection reason is required (maximum 500 characters) to explain to the contributor why the article was declined and provide guidance for revision and resubmission.

The operation updates the article's status to 'rejected', records the moderator performing the rejection, and stores the rejection_reason in the article record for contributor reference. An immutable audit trail entry is automatically created in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table with action_type 'rejected' and the rejection reason, providing permanent compliance documentation and accountability tracking.

Security context: Only authenticated moderators can invoke this operation. The moderator's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token. Articles must be in pending_approval status to be rejected; attempting to reject articles in other statuses will result in validation errors. The rejection reason provides critical feedback helping contributors understand how to revise their article for future resubmission.

Related operations: Before rejecting, moderators typically retrieve pending articles using the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles with status filter). The approval endpoint (POST /articles/{articleId}/approve) is used if the moderator determines the article meets community standards. After rejection, contributors can edit their article and resubmit for review.

Operating on the discussion_board_articles table, this action updates the article status to 'archived' and creates an audit trail entry in discussion_board_article_moderation_history. Only moderators can archive articles. Archived articles remain accessible to moderators but are hidden from contributor and public views, supporting content lifecycle management and compliance retention requirements.
operations.summary: Archive a discussion board article and remove it from active listings
operations.description:
Perform a moderation action to archive a discussion board article. This operation transitions an article from published or pending_approval status to archived status, effectively removing it from user-facing listings and search results while maintaining the complete record in the system for audit and compliance purposes.

Archiving is a reversible moderation action that moderators use to manage content visibility without permanent deletion. Archived articles are no longer discoverable through normal browsing and search, but remain queryable by moderators for historical review and audit trail purposes. The article's view count and comment history are preserved.

This operation requires moderator-level permissions and creates an immutable audit trail entry recording the archival action, timestamp, and moderating user. The archival action is tracked in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for complete accountability and compliance documentation of all moderator decisions affecting articles.

Only articles with status 'published' or 'pending_approval' can be archived. Articles already in 'archived', 'rejected', 'draft', or 'deleted' status cannot be archived. The operation returns the complete updated article record reflecting the new archived status and updated_at timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the article to archive

requestBody.description: Archival action details including moderator's removal reason for compliance documentation

responseBody.description: Complete article record with updated status set to 'archived' and current moderation state

Operating on the discussion_board_articles table, this action sets the is_pinned flag to true and creates an audit trail entry in discussion_board_article_moderation_history. Only moderators can pin articles. Pinned articles appear before all unpinned articles in browsing and search views, increasing visibility and reader engagement with moderator-selected content.
operations.summary: Pin a discussion board article to featured display at top of listings
operations.description:
Perform a moderation action to pin a discussion board article to the top of content listings for featured visibility. This operation marks the article as pinned, causing it to appear above all unpinned articles in category browsing, search results, and article listings throughout the discussion board interface.

Pinning is a curation tool that moderators use to highlight high-quality discussions, important announcements, or particularly valuable contributor insights. Pinned articles maintain their original publication date and sorting but are sorted to the top of result sets to ensure maximum visibility. Multiple articles can be pinned simultaneously, with their relative order determined by secondary sort criteria.

This operation requires moderator-level permissions and creates an immutable audit trail entry recording the pinning action, timestamp, and moderating user in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table. The pinning action is reversible through the unpin operation, allowing moderators to adjust featured content as discussions evolve and new topics emerge.

Only articles with status 'published' can be pinned. Articles with status 'draft', 'pending_approval', 'rejected', 'archived', or 'deleted' cannot be pinned. The operation returns the complete updated article record reflecting the pinned status and updated_at timestamp.

responseBody.description: Complete article record with updated is_pinned flag set to true and current state

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_pinned boolean field. Only moderators can perform this action. The operation represents a moderator decision to remove an article from featured display, making it appear in normal chronological order with other articles. This action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as an audit trail entry.
operations.summary: Unpin a featured article from discussion board listings
operations.description:
Remove a pinned article from featured display at the top of article listings. This moderator action returns the article to normal chronological sorting with other articles.

Pinned articles are featured prominently in all browsing and search views. Unpinning removes this special status. The article remains published and visible in normal listings, but will no longer appear at the top. This operation is available only to authenticated moderators with full moderation permissions.

The unpinning action is recorded in the moderation history audit trail with the moderator's ID, timestamp, and action type (unpinned). The article's is_pinned field is updated to false. Related operations include locking articles (POST /articles/{articleId}/lock) and archiving articles for complete removal from listings.

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_locked boolean field. Only moderators can perform this action. Locking prevents new comments from being posted on the article while maintaining visibility of existing discussion. This action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as an audit trail entry.
operations.summary: Lock an article to prevent new comments
operations.description:
Lock an article to prevent new comments while keeping the article and existing comments visible to users. This moderator action is used to end discussion on sensitive or resolved topics while preserving the historical record.

Locked articles remain fully visible in listings and search results with all existing comments intact. Users cannot post new comments on locked articles, but can still view the existing discussion. The is_locked field is updated to true. This operation is available only to authenticated moderators with full moderation permissions.

The locking action is recorded in the moderation history audit trail with the moderator's ID, timestamp, and action type (locked). This creates an immutable record for compliance and accountability purposes. Related operations include pinning articles for featured display (POST /articles/{articleId}/pin) and archiving articles for complete removal from public listings.

operations.specification: This operation unlocks a discussion board article, enabling contributors to post new comments on the article again. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_locked boolean field. Only moderators with appropriate permissions can perform this action. The article must exist and be in a locked state. Upon successful unlock, the article becomes available for new comment submissions while preserving all existing comments and article content. This is a moderator-controlled action that reverses a prior lock operation, typically performed when moderation of discussions has concluded or when a lock was applied in error.
operations.summary: Unlock a discussion board article to allow new comments
operations.description:
Unlock a discussion board article, enabling contributors to post new comments on it again.

This operation allows moderators to remove comment restrictions from articles that were previously locked. Locked articles remain visible with all existing comments intact, but new comments cannot be posted. Unlocking restores the article to an open state where contributors can resume discussions.

The operation directly modifies the is_locked field in the discussion_board_articles table, setting it from true to false. This is a straightforward state transition that does not affect the article's content, publication status, or existing comments. The article must be in a published state and currently locked for this operation to succeed.

Moderator authentication is required for this privileged operation. The action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as a moderation decision for audit and compliance purposes. This enables complete tracking of all moderation actions taken on articles throughout their lifecycle.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to unlock

responseBody.description: The unlocked article with all metadata and current state

operations.name: unlock

prerequisites.description: Article must exist before it can be unlocked. The POST /discussionBoard/contributor/articles operation creates a new article and returns its ID, which is required for the unlock operation to reference the correct article.

operations.specification: This operation uploads and attaches a file to a discussion board article. It operates on the discussion_board_article_attachments table, creating a new attachment record linked to the parent article. Contributors can attach images (jpg, png, gif, webp) and documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) to accompany their articles, with strict file size limits enforced (5MB for images, 25MB for documents). The operation stores file metadata including original filename, file type, MIME type, file size, and a display URL for accessing the attachment in the web interface. Multiple attachments per article are supported up to a maximum of 10 files. Attachments are managed through article operations and are automatically removed when the parent article is deleted.
operations.summary: Upload and attach a file to a discussion board article
operations.description:
Upload and attach a file to a discussion board article for supporting evidence, visual content, or supplementary documents.

This operation allows contributors to attach files to their articles during creation or editing. Supported file types include images (jpg, png, gif, webp) and documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) with appropriate file size restrictions. Images are limited to 5MB while documents can be up to 25MB. operations.description:
This operation provides moderators access to the article review queue with comprehensive filtering and sorting capabilities. The moderation queue is the central workflow mechanism where submitted articles await moderator approval, rejection, or revision requests.

Moderators use this endpoint to view pending articles in a prioritized queue, allowing them to focus on high-priority submissions first. The queue displays articles submitted by contributors, showing submission timestamp, assigned moderator (if any), priority level (normal, high, or low), and any contributor notes explaining the article or addressing previous feedback. Articles are retrieved from the discussion_board_moderation_queue table along with related article and contributor information.

The operation supports advanced filtering to help moderators manage their workflow efficiently. Moderators can filter by priority level (normal/high/low) to focus on urgent reviews, filter by submission date range to view recent or older articles, filter by assigned moderator to see their own queue, and filter by contributor to review articles from specific authors. Sorting options allow viewing the queue in standard FIFO order (oldest submissions first) or by priority level.

Security and Authorization: Only authenticated moderators can access this endpoint. The operation enforces moderator-only access through authorizationActors. The response includes only information necessary for queue management, excluding sensitive contributor data beyond username and article count.

Workflow Context: This operation is typically the first step in the moderation workflow. After retrieving queue items from this endpoint, moderators proceed to GET /moderation/queue/{queueId} to view full article details, then use PUT endpoints to approve or reject articles. Moderators may also reference the contributor's violation history via GET /moderation/violations/{contributorId} to assess whether violations inform the review decision.

Pagination and Performance: Results are paginated to handle queues with many pending articles. The operation returns pagination metadata including current page, total pages, and total queue item count, enabling efficient navigation through large review queues.

Response Includes: Each queue item includes article ID, article title, contributor username, submission timestamp, review status (unreviewed/in-progress), assigned moderator name, priority level, and contributor submission notes. The discussion_board_content_violation_records table maintains an audit trail of all policy breaches detected in articles and comments, supporting violation history tracking and escalation decisions. This operation enables moderators to view violation history for specific contributors or all violations system-wide, with filtering by violation type, severity level, action taken, and date range. Results can be sorted by detection date or severity level. The operation is exclusively accessible to moderators and provides critical context for account restriction and suspension decisions by showing violation patterns and enforcement history.
operations.summary: Retrieve filtered and paginated list of content policy violations with enforcement history and contributor context
operations.description:
This operation provides moderators access to violation records across the platform, enabling comprehensive monitoring of content policy enforcement and contributor behavior patterns. The violation records table maintains a complete, immutable audit trail of every policy violation detected in articles and comments, creating institutional memory of enforcement actions.

Moderators use this endpoint to review violation history for contributors, guiding decisions about progressive escalation (warnings → restrictions → suspensions). Each violation record includes the type of violation (hate speech, personal attack, misinformation, harassment, spam, off-topic, graphic content, threats, copyright, other), severity classification (minor/moderate/severe), violation description with specific examples, enforcement action taken (edited/removed/warned/restricted/suspended/escalated), and detection timestamp.

The operation supports powerful filtering to enable targeted violation analysis. Moderators can filter by violation type to identify patterns (e.g., repeated misinformation violations), filter by contributor to review their complete violation history, filter by severity level to focus on serious violations, filter by action taken to verify enforcement consistency, and filter by date range to see recent or historical violations. These filters combine to support sophisticated violation pattern analysis.

Security and Authorization: Only authenticated moderators can access this endpoint. The response includes violation details necessary for moderation decisions but does not expose confidential moderator deliberations or internal investigation notes. Moderators can view all violations system-wide for oversight and learning purposes.

Violation Escalation Context: Violations form the foundation of contributor account management. The violation history directly informs moderation decisions: first violation typically results in warning, second violation within 30 days results in temporary restrictions, third violation within 30 days triggers suspension review. This endpoint enables moderators to quickly assess violation history and make consistent escalation decisions. The complete audit trail supports appeals and administrative oversight of moderation consistency.

Content Snapshot and Enforcement Tracking: Each violation record includes a content snapshot (first 500 characters) of the violating content at time of detection, preserving evidence even if the original content was edited or deleted. This enables moderators to verify that enforcement was appropriate. The action_details field captures specifics of moderator response (what was edited, warning message text, restriction duration).

Pagination and Performance: Results are paginated to handle systems with thousands of violation records. The operation returns pagination metadata including current page, total pages, total violation count, and optional aggregation data (count by violation type, count by contributor, severity distribution) for analytical insights into enforcement patterns.

Response Includes: Each violation record includes violation type, severity level, violation description, content snapshot, action taken and details, contributor username, detection timestamp, and linked article/comment reference. This information enables comprehensive violation review without additional queries.

operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered list of moderator audit log entries that track all moderation actions performed on the platform. This operation provides deep visibility into moderation decisions, enabling compliance review, dispute investigation, and moderation quality analysis.

The operation supports advanced filtering across multiple dimensions including action type (article_approved, article_rejected, article_deleted, comment_removed, user_warned, user_suspended, etc.), moderator who performed the action, contributor affected by the action, specific articles or comments involved, date ranges, and textual reasons. Alternative sorting by action type or moderator provides different analytical perspectives.

Security considerations include role-based access restrictions (moderators only) to prevent unauthorized visibility of sensitive moderation decisions and reasoning. The audit log is read-only from the API perspective; audit records are only created through moderation actions and never modified or deleted, ensuring immutability and integrity of the compliance record.

The operation integrates with the discussion_board_moderator_audit_log table as defined in the Prisma schema, providing visibility into action_type, reason, old_status, new_status, additional_metadata fields along with references to the moderator, affected contributor, and related article/comment. This operation provides moderators visibility into all enforcement actions taken against contributor accounts, enabling tracking of restriction status, enforcement history, and policy compliance.

The operation supports filtering across multiple enforcement dimensions including affected contributor, moderator who imposed the restriction, restriction type (posting_restriction preventing article/comment submissions, temporary_suspension denying login access, permanent_ban permanently disabling account), current restriction status (active restrictions in effect, lifted restrictions manually removed early, expired restrictions that naturally concluded), and severity classification (minor for first offenses, moderate for repeated violations, severe for serious violations, permanent for irreversible bans). Date range filters enable analysis of restriction periods and enforcement patterns over time.

Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page size and sorting options. Default sorting is by imposed_at timestamp in descending order (most recent restrictions first), enabling quick identification of active and recent enforcement actions. Alternative sorting by contributor, expiration date, or severity provides different analytical perspectives for moderation review and pattern analysis.

Security considerations include role-based access (moderators only) to prevent unauthorized visibility of enforcement actions and justifications. The suspension records include lifting information and lift_reason to track restriction removal decisions, supporting appeals processes and early release programs for rehabilitated contributors.

The operation integrates with the discussion_board_user_suspensions table as defined in the Prisma schema, providing access to suspension_type, reason, severity_level, duration_days, suspended_at, expiration_at, status, lifted_at, and lift_reason fields along with references to the contributor and imposing moderator. Results can be sorted by imposition date, contributor, or restriction type to support investigation and enforcement tracking.

Active restrictions (where the current time is before the expiration date, or expiration date is null for permanent bans) prevent contributors from creating new articles or posting comments. This operation helps moderators monitor which contributors currently have active restrictions and review the history of enforcement actions for pattern analysis and account management decisions.

Related operations: POST /contributors/{contributorId}/suspend creates new suspensions, GET /contributors/{contributorId}/violations retrieves a contributor's violation history, and PUT /moderation/restrictions/{restrictionId}/lift manually lifts restrictions before their scheduled expiration.

operations.summary: Suspend or restrict a contributor account for policy violations
operations.description:
Create a new account suspension or posting restriction on a contributor account as an enforcement action for policy violations. This operation records the suspension in the discussion_board_user_suspensions table, which maintains the complete history of all account restrictions and suspensions imposed on contributors.

When a contributor has accumulated violations or committed severe violations, moderators use this operation to enforce consequences. The operation requires specifying the suspension type (posting_restriction prevents article and comment submissions; account_suspension prevents login; permanent_ban disables the account permanently), the reason for the suspension, and the severity level (minor, moderate, severe, or permanent).

For time-limited suspensions, moderators specify the duration in days (3, 7, 30, or custom durations), and the system automatically calculates the expiration timestamp. The suspension becomes immediately effective, preventing the contributor from performing restricted actions. Suspension records include the moderator who imposed the suspension and the timestamp of the action for accountability and audit trails.

The operation creates an immutable suspension record that is never deleted; suspension history is retained indefinitely for compliance and pattern analysis. Moderators can manually lift suspensions early by using a separate lift operation if the contributor demonstrates rehabilitation, but the lifting action is also recorded with reason and timestamp for accountability.

Escalation rules apply: a contributor's first major violation triggers a warning, second violation within 30 days results in a 3-day posting restriction, third violation results in a 7-day restriction, and fourth violation triggers account suspension. Severe violations (hate speech, threats, harassment) may skip escalation steps and result in immediate suspension or permanent ban.

The suspended contributor receives notification including the suspension reason, duration (if applicable), and what they must do for account recovery. Their articles and comments remain visible with attribution but authored as 'suspended user' to preserve discussion context.

The restriction prevents the contributor from creating articles or posting comments during the restriction period. For temporary restrictions, the system automatically enforces the restriction until the expiration date; moderators can manually lift restrictions early if the contributor demonstrates rehabilitation.

The operation records comprehensive restriction metadata including the restriction type, reason for enforcement, imposing moderator, and duration. Multiple restriction types are supported: posting_restriction (cannot post articles/comments), temporary_suspension (cannot login), and permanent_ban (permanent account disablement). The reason field communicates to the contributor why their account was restricted and what conduct triggered the enforcement action.

Active restrictions (where the current timestamp is before expires_at, or expires_at is null for permanent restrictions) prevent new article submissions and comment posts. The system maintains complete restriction history for compliance auditing and pattern analysis. When a new restriction is applied to a contributor with an existing active restriction, the application-level logic replaces the previous one. Contributor notifications include the restriction reason and end date for temporary restrictions.

operations.summary: Manually lift an active account restriction from a contributor

Lift an active account restriction that was previously imposed on a discussion board contributor account.

This endpoint allows authorized moderators to manually remove posting restrictions or temporary suspensions from contributor accounts before the scheduled expiration date. When a moderator determines that a previously-restricted contributor has demonstrated rehabilitation or the restriction was applied in error, they can use this operation to restore the account to normal operation immediately.

The operation updates the restriction record with the lift timestamp and the moderator who performed the action. A reason for lifting the restriction is required, which documents the decision and communicates the explanation to the contributor. After the restriction is lifted, the contributor can immediately resume creating articles and posting comments without waiting for the automatic expiration date.

Only active restrictions (where the current timestamp is before expires_at or the restriction has not yet expired) can be lifted. Permanent bans can only be lifted by senior moderators in extraordinary circumstances. The complete restriction history is preserved in the database for compliance auditing and to track enforcement patterns. If the contributor has no active restriction, the operation returns an error indicating that there is nothing to lift.

Optional device identifier for session tracking and device-level analytics.

Can be a browser fingerprint, device UUID, user agent hash, or any string that uniquely identifies the client device or browser session. Used by the system to associate multiple API requests with the same device for session continuity and usage analytics.
