If not provided, the system generates a temporary session identifier based on the request itself.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ICreate.description:
Request payload for guest user account registration.

Guest registration is a simplified, lightweight onboarding process that creates a temporary user session without requiring email addresses, passwords, account verification, or any personal information. Guest accounts enable unauthenticated visitors to browse published articles and read comments on the discussion board.

Unlike contributor or moderator accounts, guest registration has minimal required information. Only an optional device identifier for session tracking is accepted. The registration process is public and does not require authentication. Each guest registration creates a fresh, isolated session that can be used immediately.

Guest users are limited to read-only access: they can view published articles and their associated comments but cannot create articles, post comments, upload files, or perform any moderation actions. Guest sessions are temporary and managed through JWT tokens - a short-lived access token (typically 15-60 minutes) and a longer-lived refresh token (typically 7 days) for session renewal. Guests may be automatically logged out or their sessions cleaned up after extended inactivity based on system_configurations timeout settings.

id.description: Unique identifier for the guest user session. Represents the guest's temporary identity within the discussion board system.

device_identifier.description: Optional device identifier provided during guest registration for session tracking and user activity analysis. Used to associate multiple API requests with the same device/browser session.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created. Auto-generated by the system.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized.description: Guest authentication response containing guest user identifier and JWT tokens. Returned after successful guest registration or token refresh operation. Guest users receive both short-lived access tokens (valid 30 minutes) and longer-lived refresh tokens (valid 7 days) for session management. Guest sessions enable browsing and reading articles without email verification or account commitment.

refresh_token.description: Valid guest refresh token obtained from previous registration or refresh operation. Token must not be expired or revoked. Guest refresh tokens remain valid for 7 days from creation and can be used multiple times until expiration.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRefresh.description: Request to refresh an expired or expiring guest access token. The guest provides their valid refresh token to obtain a new access token, extending the session without requiring re-registration. This operation is idempotent - calling multiple times with the same refresh token produces the same result. Guest users receive both short-lived access tokens (30 minutes) and longer-lived refresh tokens (7 days) upon registration. As the access token approaches expiration, guests should call this endpoint to seamlessly continue browsing.

email.description: Email address used for authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all contributor accounts. Valid email format required (user@domain.com). Email must be verified through confirmation link before contributor can post articles or comments.

username.description: Public display name for articles and comments. Must be unique across all contributors. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only. Immutable after creation - cannot be changed after account is registered. Used for identifying article authors and commenters.

password.description: Account password for authentication. Must be at least 8 characters with uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, and special character (@, #, $, %, !, &, etc.). Passwords are securely hashed with bcrypt (minimum 12 salt rounds) before storage. Never stored plaintext in database. Must meet security requirements to ensure account protection.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR cases). IPv4 or IPv6 format. Used for security monitoring and abuse detection. Can be null if not available.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where registration was initiated. Full URL of the page from which user registered. Enables tracking of registration context and referral paths. Required field.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) indicating where user came from before registration. HTTP Referrer header value. Indicates source of traffic and how user discovered the registration page. Required field.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.ICreate.description:
Request to register a new contributor account for the discussion board. Contributor provides email, username, and secure password for account creation. Email must be unique and will require verification before full account functionality is enabled.

Password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Username must be unique, 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only, and becomes immutable after creation. The account is created with 'active' account_status and email_verified set to false.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are required for security monitoring and audit trails. IP address is optional (can be null if server extracts it), but href and referrer are mandatory to track registration context. Upon successful registration, contributor receives JWT tokens (access token valid 30 minutes, refresh token valid 7 days) and a welcome email with verification link.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated contributor account. This UUID is generated upon account creation and serves as the permanent reference for all contributor-related operations, data associations, and audit trails.

email.description: Contributor email address used for account verification and communication. Must match the email registered during account creation. This email is required to be verified before the contributor can post articles or comments. Used for password reset flows and notification delivery.

username.description: Unique username for the contributor account. This is the public display name used when the contributor creates articles or posts comments. Username is 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only, and is immutable after account creation. Cannot be changed once the account is registered.

email_verified.description: Whether the contributor's email address has been verified through confirmation link. Account cannot post articles or comments until email is verified. Verification is required during account creation flow - contributor must click the verification link sent to their email address. This field ensures only legitimate email addresses are associated with active contributor accounts.

account_status.description:
Current account status indicating the operational state of the contributor account.

**active**: Account is fully operational. Contributor can create articles, post comments, and manage their account. Only 'active' accounts can authenticate and use token refresh operations.

**suspended**: Account has been temporarily suspended by moderators for policy violations. Contributor cannot authenticate, create articles, or post comments. All articles and comments created by suspended contributors remain visible but cannot be edited or deleted during suspension. After suspension period expires, account status returns to 'active'.

**restricted**: Account has limited access restrictions imposed by moderators. May restrict posting new articles, posting comments, or both while allowing other account operations. Contributor can still view content and manage existing contributions within restrictions. Restrictions can be lifted by moderators or expire after specified duration.

**deleted**: Account has been soft-deleted by the contributor or moderators. The account record and all associated data are retained for 6 months for audit and recovery purposes. Deleted accounts cannot authenticate or access any functionality. After 6 months, deleted accounts and associated data are permanently purged from the system.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the contributor account was created in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ). This timestamp is immutable and serves as the account creation date for audit trails, account age calculations, and display purposes. Set automatically by the system upon successful account registration.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification in ISO 8601 format. Updated when email address, password, or account status changes. Not updated on login, session creation, or article/comment creation. Used to track when account information was last changed for audit purposes.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when contributor account was deleted (soft delete) in ISO 8601 format. Null for active, suspended, or restricted accounts. Set to current timestamp when account is deleted by contributor request or moderator action. Account data is retained for 6 months from deletion to enable recovery; after 6 months, account and all associated data are permanently purged from the system.

last_login_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful login in ISO 8601 format. Null if account has never been successfully authenticated. Updated automatically upon each successful login. Not updated on failed login attempts to prevent information disclosure. Useful for identifying inactive accounts and security monitoring.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated contributor response with JWT tokens for session management.

This DTO is returned after successful contributor authentication via the join (registration), login, or refresh operations. It contains the authenticated contributor's identity information along with JWT access and refresh tokens for subsequent authenticated API requests.

The response includes the contributor's unique identifier (id), email address, username, email verification status, and current account status. The account_status field indicates the contributor's operational state: 'active' for normal operation, 'suspended' for temporary bans, 'restricted' for limited access, or 'deleted' for soft-deleted accounts. Clients should check account_status and handle different states appropriately - only 'active' accounts should proceed with normal operations without restrictions.

The token structure contains an access token (valid for 30 minutes) for making authenticated API requests with the Authorization header (Bearer scheme), and a refresh token (valid for 7 days) for obtaining new tokens when the access token expires. Clients should store the refresh token securely (localStorage in browsers, secure storage in mobile apps) and use it automatically to refresh tokens before expiration, maintaining continuous authenticated access without requiring the user to re-enter credentials. When refresh token expires (after 7 days), the contributor must re-authenticate using the login operation.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.ILogin.description:
Contributor authentication credentials for login.

Required fields to authenticate an existing contributor account. The operation validates email/username and password against stored bcrypt hash and confirms account is active with verified email.

Password is transmitted in plaintext over HTTPS and compared against bcrypt hash on server. Passwords must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Failed authentication attempts do not expose specific failure reasons for security.

email.description: Email address used for authentication. Must match exactly with contributor account email (case-insensitive matching). Account must exist in discussion_board_contributors table.

password.description: Plain text password for verification. Compared against bcrypt hash stored in discussion_board_contributors.password_hash. Must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract from request, but client may provide for SSR cases). IPv4 or IPv6 format when provided.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where login was initiated. Required for session context tracking. Used to identify session origination context.

referrer.description: HTTP Referrer URL (previous page URL) from login request. Required for session context tracking. Indicates where contributor came from before logging in.

refreshToken.description: Valid refresh token obtained from a previous authentication or token refresh operation. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days from session creation. The token must be associated with an active contributor session in the discussion_board_contributor_sessions table.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for obtaining new JWT tokens.

This DTO is used when a contributor needs to renew their authentication tokens without re-entering their credentials. The endpoint validates the provided refresh token against the contributor's session record in the discussion_board_contributor_sessions table.

The refresh token must be valid (not expired - tokens expire 7 days from session creation) and the associated contributor account must maintain 'active' status. If the account has been suspended, restricted, or deleted since the session was created, the refresh request is denied.

Upon successful validation, new access and refresh tokens are issued with extended expiration times. The access token is valid for 30 minutes for API access, and the new refresh token is valid for 7 days for future token renewals.

email.description: Moderator email address for account verification and communication. Must be unique across all moderator accounts and follow valid email format (user@domain.com).

password.description: Moderator account password. Plain text password that must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Backend hashes with bcrypt (12 salt rounds) before storing in password_hashed column.

username.description: Unique moderator username for account identification. Must be 3-50 characters containing only alphanumeric characters and underscores. No spaces or special characters allowed.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ICreate.description:
Moderator account creation request.

This DTO is used to register new moderator accounts in the discussion board system. The operation creates a new entry in the discussion_board_moderators table with administrative permissions for content moderation and user management.

Email must be unique across all moderator accounts and follows valid email format. Username must also be unique, constrained to 3-50 characters, and contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores. Password must meet complexity requirements with a minimum of 8 characters including uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

The operation stores a bcrypt-hashed password with minimum 12 salt rounds for security. The newly created moderator account is assigned 'full' moderation tier (all moderation permissions) and initialized with account_status as 'active'. However, email_verified is set to false initially, and the moderator cannot fully access moderation tools until verifying their email address through a confirmation link. This endpoint is public and requires no prior authentication, allowing new moderators to self-register within the system.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated moderator account.

email.description: Email address used for moderator authentication and account recovery. Must be unique across all moderator accounts.

username.description: Public display name for moderation actions and audit trail. Must be unique across all moderators. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only. Immutable after creation.

email_verified.description: Whether the moderator's email address has been verified through confirmation link. Account cannot access moderation tools until verified.

oneOf.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban from moderation), 'deleted' (marked for deletion).
Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban from moderation), 'deleted' (marked for deletion).
Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban from moderation), 'deleted' (marked for deletion).

account_status.description: Current account status. Valid values: 'active' (normal operation), 'suspended' (temporary ban from moderation), 'deleted' (marked for deletion).

moderation_tier.description: Moderator permission level. Current value: 'full' (all moderation permissions). Reserved for future role differentiation.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification in ISO 8601 format.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when moderator account was deleted (soft delete). Null for active accounts. Retained for compliance purposes.

last_login_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful login to moderation dashboard. Null if account has never been logged in.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated moderator response with JWT access and refresh tokens after successful login, registration, or token refresh.

Contains the moderator's unique identifier and JWT token information needed for authenticated API requests. The access token is used in Authorization headers for subsequent moderation operations. The refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens without re-entering credentials.

email.description: Moderator email address for authentication. Must match the email registered in the discussion_board_moderators table and be verified (email_verified = true). Email format must be valid (user@domain.com).

password.description: Moderator password in plain text for credential verification. The password is validated against the bcrypt-hashed password_hash field stored in the database. Must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking (OPTIONAL - server can extract from request context, but client may provide for SSR scenarios). Valid IP address format (IPv4 or IPv6) when provided.

href.description: Connection URL representing the current page URL from which the login request was initiated. This field is MANDATORY and used for session audit trail and security tracking.

referrer.description: Referrer URL representing the previous page URL that led to the current login page. This field is MANDATORY and used for session context and referral tracking. Can be empty string for direct access.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ILogin.description:
Moderator authentication request with email and password credentials.

This DTO is used for authenticating existing moderators to the discussion board system. It accepts the moderator's registered email address and password for credential-based authentication.

The email address must match an existing moderator account in the discussion_board_moderators table and be verified (email_verified = true). The password is provided in plain text and validated against the bcrypt-hashed password_hash field in the database. All moderator passwords must meet complexity requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

Authentication requires the moderator account to have account_status = 'active'. Suspended or deleted moderator accounts are rejected from login.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) capture connection metadata for audit trail purposes. The href and referrer fields are mandatory and represent the current page URL and previous page URL respectively. The ip field is optional and represents the client IP address (server can extract this from request context, but client may provide for SSR scenarios).

Upon successful authentication, the operation returns IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized with JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated access to moderation features.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token issued during prior authentication (login or registration). Used to obtain a new access token for continued authenticated access to moderation features without re-entering credentials.

The refresh token is validated against the moderator's active session in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. If the token is invalid, expired, or the associated moderator account has been suspended or deleted, the refresh attempt is rejected.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing a moderator's JWT access token using a valid refresh token.

This operation accepts a refresh token previously issued during login or registration. The refresh token is validated to ensure it is valid, has not expired, and belongs to an existing active and email-verified moderator account. Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued for continued authenticated access to moderation features.

The operation checks that the moderator's account_status is 'active' and email_verified is true. If either condition fails, the token refresh is rejected to prevent access by suspended or unverified accounts.

email.description:
Email address of the contributor account for which password reset is requested. Must be a valid email format and match a registered contributor account.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent brute-force enumeration attacks. The operation does not reveal whether an email address is registered in the system to prevent account enumeration. The response is generic regardless of whether the email exists or account status.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordResetRequest.ICr.description:
Request body for initiating a password reset request for a contributor account.

This operation validates that the provided email address exists in the system and generates a secure, time-limited token for password recovery. The password reset token is sent via email to the registered address and is valid for exactly 30 minutes from generation.

The token is single-use and becomes invalid after one successful password reset or after the 30-minute expiration window closes. If a contributor requests multiple resets, only the most recent token remains valid.

Contributors with suspended or deleted accounts cannot request password resets, and the system returns generic responses for these cases to avoid leaking account status information.

IDiscussionBoardPasswordReset.ICreate.description:
Request to reset a contributor's password using a valid reset token.

This DTO represents the second step of the password reset workflow. It accepts a reset token that was previously generated by the request-password-reset endpoint and the new password that will replace the old one.

The reset token must be valid (not expired, not previously used) and must have been generated within 30 minutes. The new password must meet strict security requirements: minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character. Passwords cannot match the contributor's previous password to prevent credential reuse.

Upon successful submission, the new password is hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds and replaces the old password. The password_changed_at timestamp is updated, and all existing sessions for the contributor are invalidated, requiring re-authentication on all devices.

reset_token.description: Valid reset token generated by the request-password-reset endpoint. Must not be expired (valid for 30 minutes from generation) or previously used. Token validity is cryptographically verified before processing. If token is invalid, expired, or already consumed, the operation is rejected with security-conscious error messaging that does not reveal specific failure reason.

new_password.description: New password for the contributor account. Must be at least 8 characters in length and include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character. Password strength validation occurs before hashing. Cannot match the contributor's previous password to prevent reuse of recently compromised credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account (contributor or moderator). Generated as UUID v4 on account creation.

email.description: Email address used for authentication and account recovery. Unique across all accounts of the same user type. Must follow RFC 5321 email format standards (user@domain.com).

username.description: Public display name used in articles, comments, and moderation actions. Unique across accounts of the same user type. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only. Immutable after creation.

emailVerified.description: Whether the user's email address has been verified through confirmation link. Accounts cannot post articles or comments until email verification is completed.

accountStatus.description: Current account status indicating user capability and access permissions. 'active' allows normal operation including posting articles and comments. 'suspended' is a temporary ban preventing all platform access, used for serious policy violations. 'restricted' allows limited posting capabilities with moderation review required. 'deleted' marks the account for soft deletion while retaining data for audit purposes and potential recovery within 6 months.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ).

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent account modification. Updated when email, username, password, or status changes. Not updated on session creation or content posting.

lastLoginAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful login. Null if account has never been logged in. Updated only on successful authentication, not on failed attempts.

passwordChangedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent password change. Null if password has never been changed from initial setup. All active sessions are invalidated when password changes for security enforcement.

deletedAt.description: Timestamp when the account was soft-deleted. Null for active accounts. Retained for 6 months to enable account recovery; after 6 months, accounts marked for deletion can be permanently purged from the system. Soft deletion preserves all associated content and audit trails for compliance.

moderationTier.description: For moderator accounts only: permission level for moderation actions. Current value is 'full' for all permissions granting access to all moderation features. Null for contributor accounts, as contributors do not have moderation capabilities.

IDiscussionBoardUser.description:
User account information for discussion board contributors and moderators.

Represents the core user profile data returned in API responses for both contributor and moderator accounts. Includes authentication identity, account status, and profile metadata while excluding sensitive data like password hashes and session tokens. This unified type accommodates both user types with role-specific fields: contributors have null moderationTier, while moderators have a defined tier value.

The account lifecycle includes creation, verification, active operation, potential restrictions or suspension by moderators, and eventual soft deletion with audit trail preservation. All timestamps are recorded in ISO 8601 format for audit compliance and system integration.

Used in responses for profile retrieval and update operations. Never includes password_hash or session information. Supports audit trail queries through timestamp fields and enables account recovery within the 6-month soft deletion window.

email.description: New email address for the account. Must be unique across all accounts of the same user type. Must follow RFC 5321 email format standards (user@domain.com). Email changes may trigger re-verification requirement if configured.

username.description: New public display name for articles, comments, and moderation context. Must be unique across accounts of the same user type. 3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only (pattern: ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{3,50}$). Note: Field is accepted in update requests for API consistency, but username is immutable after account creation per business rules.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating authenticated user's profile information.

Accepts updates to user account details such as email address and username. All fields are optional to support partial updates where users can modify one or more fields atomically. The operation validates uniqueness constraints and format requirements before persisting changes.

Email updates must be unique across accounts of the same user type and follow valid email format. Duplicate email values will result in HTTP 409 Conflict error. Username updates must be unique and match the required pattern; duplicates also result in HTTP 409 Conflict.

The system automatically records the update timestamp (updated_at) when changes are applied. Password changes are NOT handled through this operation - they use a dedicated password change endpoint with additional verification. Account status, moderation_tier, and other administrative fields cannot be modified through this operation.

Security: User can only update their own profile via authenticated request. Validation failures prevent any partial updates - either all changes succeed or none are persisted.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IChangePassw.description:
Request body for changing a contributor's account password.

Allows authenticated contributors to update their account password by providing their current password for verification and specifying the new password. The new password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character.

The current password is verified against the Bcrypt-hashed password_hash stored in the discussion_board_contributors table to prevent unauthorized password changes. Upon successful password change, the password_changed_at timestamp is updated, and all active sessions for the contributor are invalidated immediately for security purposes, requiring re-authentication on all devices.

current_password.description: Current password for verification. Must match the contributor's current password to prevent unauthorized changes. Required to confirm the contributor's identity before allowing password modification.

new_password.description: New password that must meet security requirements. Minimum 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter (A-Z), one lowercase letter (a-z), one number (0-9), and one special character (!@#$%^&*-_=+). The password will be hashed using Bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds before storage in the password_hash field.

password_confirmation.description: Confirmation of the new password to prevent typos. Must exactly match the new_password field. Used for client-side validation to ensure the contributor enters the intended password correctly.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IPasswordCha.description:
Response confirming successful password change for a contributor account.

Returned after a contributor successfully changes their account password through the POST /discussionBoard/contributor/profile/change-password endpoint. Indicates that the password has been updated in the discussion_board_contributors table (password_hash field), the password_changed_at timestamp has been set to the current time, and all active sessions have been invalidated for security purposes.

The contributor must log in again on all devices with their new password, as all existing session tokens have been revoked. This operation does not affect other account properties or data.

success.description: Indicates whether the password change operation completed successfully. Always true in a success response.

message.description: Human-readable confirmation message indicating the password has been successfully changed. Example: 'Your password has been changed successfully. You will be logged out on all devices for security purposes.'

changed_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 format) when the password change was completed and recorded in the password_changed_at field. Used for audit trail and security event tracking.

sessions_invalidated.description: Indicates whether all active sessions for this contributor have been invalidated. Always true, requiring the contributor to re-authenticate on all devices with the new password.

password.description: Plain text password for verification. Required to authorize account deletion to prevent unauthorized or accidental deletion. Must match the current account password.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IDeleteAccou.description:
Request body for contributor account deletion with password verification.

Requires password verification as a security measure to prevent accidental or unauthorized account deletion. The operation performs soft deletion by setting deleted_at timestamp and changing account_status to 'deleted', preserving all data for audit and recovery.

success.description: Whether the account deletion was successful

message.description: Confirmation message indicating the account has been marked for deletion

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the account deletion was processed in ISO 8601 format

IDiscussionBoardContributor.IDeleteAccou.description:
Response body confirming successful account deletion.

Indicates that the contributor account has been soft-deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp and changing account_status to 'deleted'. All account data is preserved in the database for audit trails and recovery purposes. The contributor can no longer log in or access any features. Articles and comments created remain visible but associated with the deleted contributor account.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.description:
Registered contributor user account for the discussion board.

Stores authentication credentials, profile information, and account status for contributors who can create articles and post comments. Each contributor account is unique by email and username.

Password security is enforced through bcrypt hashing with minimum 12 salt rounds. Email addresses are stored for authentication flows (login, password reset, notifications). Account creation requires email verification before enabling login.

Contributors maintain separate session management from moderators for security isolation. Violation history and account restrictions track contributor standing and enforcement actions. Soft deletion preserves contributor information while enabling account recovery within 6 months.

IDiscussionBoardContributor.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a contributor for reference contexts.

Provides essential contributor identification information when embedding contributor references in audit logs, violation records, and other contexts where full contributor details are unnecessary.

Includes only the unique identifier and display name to keep response payloads compact while enabling user identification. Used in nested references throughout the moderation system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the contributor account. Primary key reference enabling system-wide identification and linking of contributor records.

username.description: Display name of the contributor shown throughout the platform. Used for user identification in UI contexts and audit logs. Provides human-readable reference without exposing full profile information.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the article, generated automatically as UUID primary key.

Serves as the primary key in the discussion_board_articles table and is immutable after creation. Used in all API operations to reference specific articles.

title.description:
Article title displayed in listings, search results, and article headers.

Between 5 and 200 characters describing the article topic. Provides concise identification of article subject matter for users browsing or searching discussions. Examples: 'Analysis of Recent Economic Policy Changes', 'Political Governance in Modern Systems'.

content.description:
Article body content in plain text or markdown format.

Between 50 and 50,000 characters containing the main discussion, analysis, opinion, or information. Represents the core contribution to the discussion platform. Supports formatting and rich expression of ideas.

oneOf.description: Draft status: Article in progress, not yet submitted for moderation. Visible only to author and moderators. Author can freely edit content, title, and category. Transitions to pending_approval when author submits for review or to deleted when author removes the article.

Pending approval status: Article submitted for moderator review. Visible only to author and moderators. Moderators can approve (→published) or reject (→rejected). Author cannot edit while pending. Represents articles awaiting content review against community guidelines.

Published status: Article approved and publicly visible. Visible to all users (guests, contributors, moderators). Comments can be posted unless article is locked. Can be archived or pinned by moderators. Represents articles that have passed moderation and are actively contributing to discussions.

Rejected status: Moderator declined publication. Visible only to author and moderators. Rejection reason provided for author guidance. Author can edit and resubmit for review. Represents articles not meeting community standards and awaiting revision.

Archived status: Removed from active listings and public browsing. Visible only to moderators for historical reference. Comments cannot be added. Can be restored by moderators. Represents articles preserved for compliance while no longer actively discussed.

Deleted status: Soft-deleted through moderator or author action. Hidden from regular users. Moderators can view for audit trail. Preserves record for compliance. Represents articles removed from discussion but retained for historical documentation.

status.description:
Current publication status of the article, determining visibility and available actions.

Valid values: draft (in progress), pending_approval (awaiting moderator review), published (approved and public), rejected (moderator declined), archived (removed from active listings), deleted (soft-deleted for compliance). Article lifecycle progresses through: draft → pending_approval → published (or rejected → pending_approval). Published articles can be archived or deleted.

Status determines who can view the article, what edits are permitted, when comments can be posted, and whether the article appears in public listings.

author.description:
The contributor who created and authored the article.

References the contributor account that originally submitted the article. Immutable after article creation. Identifies the original author for attribution and contact purposes. Separate from lastEditedByContributor which tracks subsequent edits.

category.description:
Article category for organizational classification and browsing.

References one of the predefined article categories (Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation, International, Analysis, Opinion, Other Discussion). Required for all articles. Enables users to browse articles by topic area. Can be changed by contributor or moderator before publication.

approvedByModerator.description:
Moderator who approved the article for publication, if applicable.

References the moderator account that transitioned the article from pending_approval to published status. Null if article has not yet been approved. Immutable once set. Records accountability for editorial approval decisions. Used for audit trail and attribution of moderation actions.

lastEditedByContributor.description:
Contributor or moderator who last edited the article content or metadata, if applicable.

References the user account that performed the most recent modification to article properties. Null if article has never been edited after creation. Tracks editorial history for audit purposes. Distinguishes original author from subsequent revisors.

created_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the article was originally created by the contributor.

Set automatically on article creation and is immutable thereafter. Reflects when the author first saved the draft. Used for sorting articles chronologically and establishing creation order in discussion threads.

updated_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent modification to any article field.

Updated whenever article properties change (content, title, category, status, moderation flags). Tracks editorial activity and helps identify recently active discussions. Used for sorting and identifying updated content.

published_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the article was approved and published by moderator, if applicable.

Set automatically when moderator approves article, transitioning status to published. Null if article has not yet been approved. Immutable once set. Marks the moment article became publicly visible. Distinct from created_at to distinguish drafting from publication.

deleted_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the article was soft-deleted, if applicable.

Set when article is removed by author or moderator. Null if article is not deleted. Immutable once set (deletion is permanent). Soft deletion preserves the record for audit trail, compliance, and historical reference while removing public visibility.

approval_notes.description:
Optional moderator feedback provided during article approval.

Maximum 1,000 characters of constructive feedback from the approving moderator. Visible to the article author and other moderators. Null if article has not been approved. Provides context for why article was approved and suggestions for future contributions.

rejection_reason.description:
Moderator explanation for article rejection, if applicable.

Maximum 500 characters explaining why the article does not meet community guidelines or standards. Visible to the article author to guide revision and resubmission. Null if article has not been rejected. Provides critical feedback helping contributors understand how to improve their work.

view_count.description:
Denormalized count of user views on the article.

Starts at zero and increments with each article access. Used to identify popular and trending discussions without requiring expensive comment joins. Helps moderators identify valuable community contributions. Reset to zero if article is deleted.

comment_count.description:
Denormalized cached count of published comments on the article.

Maintained in sync with actual comment records for efficient display in article listings without querying comment table. Starts at zero. Incremented when comments are published, decremented when comments are deleted. Provides engagement indicator for article popularity.

is_pinned.description:
Whether the article is pinned to the top of listings for featured display.

Set by moderators to highlight high-quality discussions, important announcements, or valuable insights. Pinned articles appear above unpinned articles in all browsing views and search results. Defaults to false. Represents a temporary curation decision, reversible through unpin operation.

is_locked.description:
Whether the article is locked from further comments and edits.

Set by moderators to end discussion on sensitive or resolved topics while preserving existing comments and article visibility. Users cannot post new comments on locked articles but can view all existing discussion. Defaults to false. Used for lifecycle management and discussion closure.

attachments.description:
File attachments (images and documents) associated with the article.

Optional array of attachment metadata including original filename, file type, size, MIME type, upload timestamp, and display URL. Populated when article is retrieved with full details. Empty array if article has no attachments. Maximum 10 attachments per article. Attachments are pre-uploaded to storage with display URLs provided.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Complete article entity representing economic and political discussion content created by contributors.

Core entity in the discussion board system storing articles submitted by contributors for community discussion and moderator review. Each article contains discussion content, metadata, author information, publication status, and moderation tracking.

Article lifecycle: Contributors create articles in draft status and save work before submission. When ready, articles transition to pending_approval for moderator review against community guidelines. Moderators approve articles to published status for public visibility, or reject for revision. Published articles can be pinned for featured display, locked to prevent new comments, or archived when discussions conclude. Soft deletion preserves articles for compliance audit trails.

Relationships: Each article references a contributor author, article category, and optionally a moderator approver. Articles can have multiple file attachments and associated comments from community members. Moderation history is tracked in separate audit tables for accountability.

Moderation capabilities include approval with feedback notes, rejection with guidance, pinning for curation, locking for discussion closure, and archival for lifecycle management. All moderation actions create immutable audit trail entries for compliance documentation.

id.description: Unique identifier of the article.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of an article for efficient reference and embedding.

Provides essential article identification information used in contexts requiring minimal payload size: audit logs, violation records, and moderation history where only article ID and title are needed for reference.

Used when displaying articles in list contexts, moderation action records, and as foreign key references in related entities. The summary variant excludes detailed content, metadata, and moderation information to keep response payloads efficient. Full article details retrieved via main IDiscussionBoardArticle type when complete information required.

title.description: Article title describing the article topic. Required field between 5 and 200 characters. Examples: 'Analysis of Recent Economic Policy Changes', 'Political Governance in Modern Systems'.

content.description: Article body content in plain text or markdown format. Required field containing the main discussion or analysis. Must be between 50 and 50,000 characters. Represents the core discussion contribution.

categoryId.description: UUID identifier of the article category. Must reference a valid, active category from article_categories table. Required field. Examples: Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation categories.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session tracking and audit trail
Null when server extracts from request headers

ip.description: Client IP address for session context and security monitoring. Optional field - server can extract from request headers or client may provide for server-side rendering scenarios. Used for session audit trail and connection tracking when contributor creates articles.

href.description: Current page URL (connection URL) at time of article creation. Required field for session context. Represents the web page URL from which the article creation request originated. Used for session audit trail and referrer tracking.

referrer.description: Previous page URL (referrer) that led to article creation page. Required field for session context. Represents the source page that directed the user to the article creation interface. Used for session audit trail and navigation history tracking.

attachments.description: Optional file attachments (images and documents) to accompany the article. Maximum 10 files per article. Each attachment includes filename, file extension, size information, and pre-uploaded URL. File type validation is enforced: JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP for images; PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX for documents. Size limits: 10MB for images, 25MB for documents.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new article draft.

Allows authenticated contributors to compose articles on economic and political topics. Articles are initialized in 'draft' status, allowing contributors to save their work and return later to continue editing without requiring immediate moderator approval.

The authenticated contributor's ID is automatically assigned as the article author through JWT authentication context. Validation is enforced for all required fields: title 5-200 characters, content 50-50,000 characters, category must be from predefined categories. Optional attachments are supported with file type and size validation.

Session context fields (href and referrer) are required for session creation and audit trail tracking. These represent connection metadata from the client request origin, not authentication identity. The ip field is optional as servers can extract client IP from request headers, though clients may provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios.

Security: Only authenticated contributors with active accounts and verified email addresses can create articles. The system prevents contributors from creating articles on behalf of others by using the authenticated user context from JWT tokens, never from request body fields. Article author identification comes exclusively from authentication context.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1 for the first page. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used with limit to implement offset-based pagination.

limit.description: Number of articles to return per page. Defaults to 20 if not provided. Maximum 100 articles per page to prevent excessive data transfer.

status.description: Filter by article publication status. When specified, only articles with the matching status are returned. Null or omitted means no status filtering (all matching statuses returned based on authorization). Valid values: draft, pending_approval, published, rejected, archived, deleted.

categoryId.description: Filter by article category UUID. When specified, only articles assigned to this category are returned. Null or omitted means no category filtering.

contributorId.description: Filter by article author contributor UUID. When specified, only articles created by this contributor are returned. Null or omitted means no author filtering.

createdDateFrom.description: Filter by article creation date starting from this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Returns articles created on or after this date. Null or omitted means no creation date lower bound.

createdDateTo.description: Filter by article creation date up to this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Returns articles created on or before this date. Null or omitted means no creation date upper bound.

publishedDateFrom.description: Filter by article publication date starting from this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Returns articles published on or after this date. Null or omitted means no publication date lower bound. Only applies to published articles.

publishedDateTo.description: Filter by article publication date up to this ISO 8601 timestamp (inclusive). Returns articles published on or before this date. Null or omitted means no publication date upper bound. Only applies to published articles.

search.description: Full-text search query to match against article titles and content. When specified, only articles containing the search terms are returned. Case-insensitive search. Null or omitted means no text search filtering.

isPinned.description: Filter by pinned status. When true, only pinned articles are returned. When false, only unpinned articles are returned. Null or omitted means no pinned status filtering.

isLocked.description: Filter by locked status. When true, only locked articles are returned. When false, only unlocked articles are returned. Null or omitted means no locked status filtering.

orderBy.description: Sort field for ordering results. Valid options: createdAt (creation timestamp), publishedAt (publication timestamp), viewCount (popularity), commentCount (discussion activity), isPinned (featured status). Defaults to createdAt if not specified.

order.description: Sort direction for the selected orderBy field. Valid values: asc (ascending), desc (descending). Defaults to desc (most recent or highest value first).

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for article discovery.

Supports comprehensive filtering by status, category, author, date ranges, and full-text search. Pagination with configurable page size. Sorting by multiple dimensions (creation/publication date, popularity, activity, featured status).

All filter parameters are optional and independent - when multiple filters are specified, they are combined with AND logic. When filters are omitted or null, no filtering is applied for that dimension.

Used in the article list/search operation (PATCH /articles) to enable flexible article discovery.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a moderator for reference contexts.

Provides essential moderator identification information when embedding moderator references in audit logs, violation records, and other moderation-related contexts where full moderator details are unnecessary.

Includes only the unique identifier and display name to keep response payloads compact while enabling moderator identification and accountability tracking. Used in nested references throughout the moderation system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderator account. Primary key reference enabling system-wide identification and linking of moderator records and actions.

username.description: Display name of the moderator shown throughout the platform. Used for moderator identification in audit logs and moderation dashboards. Provides human-readable reference for accountability tracking.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Identifier of the parent article this attachment belongs to. Immutably linked to the article at creation time.

original_filename.description: Original filename as provided by the uploader. Maximum 255 characters. Displayed to users when downloading or viewing the attachment. Preserves the original filename for user reference.

file_type.description: File extension indicating format (e.g., jpg, png, gif, webp, pdf, docx, xlsx, txt). Used for validation, categorization, and determining display type in the UI.

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes. Used to enforce size limits (5MB for images, 25MB for documents) and display file size information to users.

mime_type.description: MIME type for proper browser display and rendering (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf). Guides the frontend on how to render or process the file.

uploaded_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when file was uploaded. Immutable after upload. Used for audit trail, sorting attachments, and recording upload history.

display_url.description: Relative or absolute URL path for accessing or displaying the attachment in the web interface. Used by frontend to create download links or embed images in article rendering.

uploaded_by_contributor.description: Summary information of the contributor who uploaded this attachment. References uploaded_by_contributor_id for audit and attribution purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description:
File attachment metadata for images and documents attached to discussion board articles.

Represents a single file attachment including metadata about the uploaded file. Attachments are immutably linked to their parent article and tracked with uploader information for audit purposes. Supports images (jpg, png, gif, webp) up to 5MB and documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) up to 25MB.

When articles are published, attachments remain accessible. When articles are deleted, all associated attachments are automatically removed. Each article supports up to 10 attachments maximum.

original_filename.description: Original filename as provided by the uploader. Maximum 255 characters. Required for user reference when downloading or viewing the attachment. The filename is displayed in the UI and used for download naming to help users understand what file they are accessing.

file_type.description: File extension indicating the file format. Allowed formats: jpg, png, gif, webp (images), pdf, docx, xlsx, txt (documents). File type validation is enforced to prevent unsupported files from being attached. The extension guides UI components on how to render or process the file appropriately.

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes. Must not exceed enforced size limits: 5MB (5,242,880 bytes) for image files, 25MB (26,214,400 bytes) for document files. Size validation occurs before storage to ensure compliance with platform storage policies and prevent excessive resource consumption.

mime_type.description: MIME type corresponding to the file format. Examples: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, text/plain. The MIME type is essential for proper browser rendering and handling of different file types when displaying or downloading attachments.

display_url.description: URL where the uploaded file is accessible. Must be a pre-uploaded URL from the storage service. The client provides the complete URL to the already-stored file. This URL is used by the web interface to create download links, embed images in articles, and provide access to attachment content without requiring additional file upload operations.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description: Request data for creating and attaching a new file to a discussion board article. Provides complete file metadata for attaching pre-uploaded files to articles. The file itself must be pre-uploaded to storage and the display_url provided. The operation validates file type against allowed formats (images: jpg, png, gif, webp; documents: pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) and file size against limits (5MB for images, 25MB for documents), records uploader information from authentication context, and links the attachment to the parent article. Each article supports up to 10 attachments maximum. When articles are published, attachments remain accessible. When articles are deleted, all associated attachments are automatically removed from both database and storage to prevent orphaned files.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update request payload for modifying discussion board articles.

Supports updates to article content, title, category assignment, and administrative metadata. Fields are all optional, allowing partial updates of only the fields being modified.

Contributor-specific updates: Contributors can update title, content, and category on their own draft or rejected articles. Moderator-specific updates: Moderators can update status, approval notes, rejection reason, pin status, and lock status on any article. System automatically updates the modified timestamp (updated_at) and tracks which user performed the edit.

title.description: Updated article title. Between 5 and 200 characters. Optional field - only include if updating title.

content.description: Updated article body content in plain text or markdown format. Between 50 and 50,000 characters. Optional field - only include if updating content.

article_category_id.description: Updated category assignment for the article. References article_categories.id. Optional field - only include if recategorizing the article.

oneOf.description: Updated publication status. Valid values: draft, pending_approval, published, rejected, archived, deleted. Used by moderators to transition articles through workflow. Optional field.

approval_notes.description: Moderator approval feedback (maximum 1,000 characters). Visible to contributor and other moderators. Used when approving articles. Optional field - only moderators can set this.

rejection_reason.description: Moderator rejection explanation (maximum 500 characters). Provided to contributor to guide revision for resubmission. Used when rejecting articles. Optional field - only moderators can set this.

is_pinned.description: Pin article to top of listings for featured display. Moderators use this to highlight important discussions. Optional field - only moderators can modify.

is_locked.description: Lock article to prevent new comments. Locked articles remain visible with existing comments but new comments are blocked. Moderators use for sensitive or resolved topics. Optional field - only moderators can modify.

approvalNotes.description: Optional moderator feedback provided during article approval. Maximum 1,000 characters. Visible to contributor and other moderators. Helps provide constructive feedback about why article was approved or suggestions for future contributions.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IApprove.description:
Moderator approval decision request for pending articles.

Request body for the article approval operation. Moderators provide optional approval notes (maximum 1,000 characters) to give constructive feedback to the contributor. The moderator's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and is not included in the request body.

The operation transitions the article from pending_approval status to published status, records the approving moderator, sets the published_at timestamp, and creates an immutable audit trail entry for compliance documentation.

rejectionReason.description: Required moderator explanation for article rejection. Maximum 500 characters. Provides critical feedback to the contributor explaining why the article does not meet community standards and how they can revise it for resubmission.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IReject.description:
Moderator rejection decision request for pending articles.

Request body for the article rejection operation. Moderators provide a required rejection reason (maximum 500 characters) to explain to the contributor why the article does not meet community guidelines or quality standards and to guide them in revising and resubmitting.

The operation transitions the article from pending_approval status to rejected status, records the rejecting moderator, stores the rejection reason, and creates an immutable audit trail entry for compliance documentation and accountability tracking.

removalReason.description: Moderator's reason for archiving the article. Maximum 500 characters. Provides documentation for compliance and audit trail purposes.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IArchive.description: Request body for archiving a discussion board article. Contains the moderator's rationale for removing the article from active listings. The archival action is reversible and preserves the article record for historical reference and compliance documentation.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the comment.

content.description: Comment text content. Required field containing the discussion contribution between 1 and 5,000 characters.

author.description: The contributor who posted this comment. Provides author context including username and account information.

article.description: The article this comment belongs to. Provides article context including title and publication status.

parentComment.description: Parent comment if this is a reply to another comment. Null for top-level comments on the article. Allows hierarchical threading of discussions.

attachments.description: Image file attachments associated with this comment. Limited to 2 files per comment. Contains all images uploaded by the contributor to provide supporting visual content for their discussion contribution. Attachments are created atomically with the comment and included in the response to enable complete comment display without additional API calls.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the comment was created. Recorded at the moment the comment is posted by the contributor.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent modification. Updated when the comment is edited by the author or moderator.

deleted_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp if comment was deleted by author or moderator. Null for active comments. Used for soft deletion to preserve thread structure.

is_deleted.description: Whether this comment has been deleted and is no longer visible. True indicates soft delete; false indicates active comment.

edit_count.description: Number of times this comment has been edited by the author or moderator. Starts at 0 when comment is created. Helps track comment history.

reply_count.description: Number of direct replies to this comment. Used for efficiently displaying reply count without querying child comments.

article_publication_status.description: Cached publication status of the parent article at the time the comment was posted (e.g., 'published', 'archived'). Immutable record providing audit context for when comment was created.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Complete comment representation including author, article context, threading information, and attachments.

Represents a user comment posted on an article or as a reply to another comment. Includes full audit trail with creation and modification timestamps, deletion status, and edit tracking.

Comments support hierarchical threading where replies to comments are linked via parentComment field. The cached article_publication_status preserves the article's state at comment creation time for audit purposes.

Deleted comments maintain their structure (soft delete) to preserve discussion thread coherence while indicating deletion status via is_deleted flag and deleted_at timestamp.

Comments include all associated image attachments (up to 2 files) that contributors uploaded with the comment. Attachments are bounded composition data created atomically with the comment. Including attachments in the response enables complete comment display without requiring separate API calls to fetch images.

id.description: Unique identifier of the comment.

content.description: The text content of the comment.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a comment for reference in audit logs and violation records.

Provides basic identification information about comments involved in moderation actions.

limit.description: Number of comments per page. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Maximum 100 to prevent excessive data transfer.

search.description: Full-text search term to filter comments by content. Searches within the comment text. Optional parameter.

author_id.description: Filter comments by specific contributor (author). Returns only comments posted by the specified contributor. Optional parameter.

created_after.description: ISO 8601 timestamp to filter comments created after this date. Useful for finding recent comments. Optional parameter.

created_before.description: ISO 8601 timestamp to filter comments created before this date. Useful for finding older comments. Optional parameter.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. 'created_at' sorts by creation time (newest first), 'reply_count' sorts by number of replies (highest first). Defaults to 'created_at'.
Field to sort results by. 'created_at' sorts by creation time (newest first), 'reply_count' sorts by number of replies (highest first). Defaults to 'created_at'.

include_deleted.description: Whether to include soft-deleted comments in results. Only applicable for moderators. Defaults to false for regular users (non-moderators).

include_nested.description: Whether to include nested replies in the response. If true, returns both top-level comments and all replies. If false, returns only top-level comments. Defaults to true.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for retrieving comments on a discussion board article.

Provides flexible query capabilities for filtering comments by content, author, date range, and sorting preferences. Supports pagination to handle large comment threads efficiently. Includes access control parameters (include_deleted) that vary based on user permissions.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new comment on a published discussion board article.

Allows authenticated contributors to post comments to existing articles, enabling community discussion and engagement. The comment is published immediately without requiring moderator approval, though moderators retain the ability to edit or remove inappropriate comments.

Comments support optional file attachments (images only) and can be nested replies to other comments or top-level comments on the article. When replying to a comment, the parentCommentId field establishes the relationship and enables proper thread organization. Top-level comments have no parent and appear at the article level.

Each comment maintains contributor attribution and optional image attachments (JPG, PNG, GIF formats), limited to 2 files per comment with 5MB size limits. The system validates attachment MIME types and stores metadata including original filenames and file sizes for proper display and storage management.

parentCommentId.description: Optional unique identifier of the parent comment when this comment is a reply to another comment. If not provided or null, this is a top-level comment on the article. When provided, establishes hierarchical threading for nested discussion organization.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.ICreat.description:
Request data for creating a new image file attachment for a discussion board comment.

Contains the metadata and file information needed to register an attachment with a specific comment. The system validates file type (images only: JPG, PNG, GIF), enforces file size limits (maximum 5MB per attachment), and validates that the MIME type matches the file extension to prevent format spoofing.

The display_url must point to the location where the uploaded image file is stored and accessible for retrieval. The contributor ID is automatically captured from the authenticated user context and is not included in this request body. The comment ID is provided as a path parameter, not in this request body.
