IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.description:
Image file attachment associated with a comment on a discussion board article.

Represents a file attachment linked to a specific comment, storing metadata about the uploaded image including the original filename, file type, size, upload timestamp, and access URL. Each comment can have up to 2 image attachments (JPG, PNG, GIF formats only) with a maximum size of 5MB per attachment.

Attachments are created when contributors upload supporting visual content to their comments to provide evidence, context, or visual references for their discussion contributions. The system tracks the uploading contributor for accountability and enables future moderation actions on attachments.

The attachment metadata enables proper file handling, validation, and display. The display_url provides the location where the image can be accessed or embedded in the web interface. Attachments are soft-deleted along with their parent comments to preserve thread structure.

content.description: Updated comment text content. Must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Contributors can edit within 24-hour window; moderators have unlimited editing authority.

attachments.description:
Optional image file attachments to create or update with this comment modification. Each comment can have up to 2 image attachments. Attachments can be added or modified atomically with the comment content update, enabling complete comment management in a single transaction.

When provided, new attachments are created and associated with the comment. File validation follows the same rules as POST /comments/{commentId}/attachments: images only (JPG, PNG, GIF), maximum 5MB per file, and MIME type validation against file type.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating comment content and managing attachments.

Allows modification of existing comment content and optional attachment management in a single atomic transaction. The comment text must be between 1 and 5,000 characters. Timestamps, edit count, and deletion status are managed by the system.

Applicable rules: Contributors can edit their own comments within a 24-hour window from creation. Moderators can edit any comment regardless of time elapsed. The system automatically updates updated_at timestamp and increments edit_count on successful modification. Edited comments are marked with edit indicator showing modification timestamp.

Attachments can be managed atomically with content updates, enabling contributors to add visual context while editing comment text in the same operation. This supports the atomic operation principle where single API calls provide complete business operations without requiring follow-up requests.

id.description: Primary key. Unique identifier for the category.

code.description: Unique machine-readable identifier for the category (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance'). Used in APIs and internal references. Must be 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the category (e.g., 'Economic Policy', 'Political Governance'). Shown in user interfaces, category listings, and article filters.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the category scope and purpose. Helps users understand which category their article should belong to. Maximum 500 characters.

display_order.description: Numeric order for displaying categories in user interfaces. Lower numbers appear first in category menus and navigation.

is_active.description: Whether this category is currently available for article submission. Active categories appear in category selection dropdowns when users create articles. Inactive categories persist for historical reference but prevent new articles from being assigned.

article_count.description: Denormalized count of published articles in this category. Used for display purposes (e.g., 'Economic Policy (47 articles)'). Updated when articles are published or unpublished.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the category was created in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified in ISO 8601 format.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the category was soft-deleted in ISO 8601 format. Null for active categories. Soft deletion preserves historical category data while removing the category from active use.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.description:
Complete article category definition with metadata and management information.

Represents predefined topic categories that organize discussion board content into logical areas. Every published article must belong to exactly one category, providing the primary organizational structure for browsing and discovery.

Categories include configuration for display order, active status to enable/disable for new submissions, and article count tracking. Soft deletion preserves historical category data when categories are deprecated while maintaining references from existing articles.

Related entities: discussion_board_articles references this table via category_id when articles are created or updated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the content guideline policy rule.

code.description: Machine-readable identifier for the guideline (e.g., 'hate-speech', 'misinformation', 'spam'). 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens. Used in moderation logs and audit trails to uniquely identify the policy rule being violated.

title.description: Short, descriptive title of the guideline (e.g., 'Hate Speech', 'Misinformation', 'Commercial Spam'). 10-100 characters. Displayed in moderation dashboards and violation notices to moderators and contributors.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the policy and what content violates it. Should include clear examples of prohibited behavior and the rationale for the policy. Maximum 2000 characters. Moderators use this when making judgment calls about borderline content and contributors reference it to understand community standards.

applies_to_articles.description: Whether this guideline applies to article content. If true, moderators review articles against this guideline during approval process. Defaults to true for most guidelines affecting discussion board articles.

applies_to_comments.description: Whether this guideline applies to comment content. If true, moderators monitor comments for violations of this guideline. Defaults to true for most guidelines affecting discussion board comments.

oneOf.description: Classification of violation severity. 'minor' violations result in edit/warning only. 'moderate' violations result in removal and warning. 'severe' violations result in content removal and account suspension. Guides moderator response proportionality and escalation decisions.

Classification of violation severity. 'minor' violations result in edit/warning only. 'moderate' violations result in removal and warning. 'severe' violations result in content removal and account suspension. Guides moderator response proportionality and escalation decisions.

Classification of violation severity. 'minor' violations result in edit/warning only. 'moderate' violations result in removal and warning. 'severe' violations result in content removal and account suspension. Guides moderator response proportionality and escalation decisions.

severity_level.description: Classification of violation severity. 'minor' violations result in edit/warning only. 'moderate' violations result in removal and warning. 'severe' violations result in content removal and account suspension. Guides moderator response proportionality and escalation decisions.

violation_consequence.description: Description of typical consequences for violating this guideline (e.g., 'comment removal', 'article rejection with feedback', 'account suspension after 3 violations'). Maximum 500 characters. Helps set contributor expectations and ensures consistent enforcement across moderators.

display_order.description: Numeric order for displaying guidelines in user-facing policy documentation. Lower numbers appear first. Defaults to 0. Used to organize guidelines by importance or category for public visibility.

is_active.description: Whether this guideline is currently enforced. Active guidelines are displayed in policy documentation and used by moderators. Inactive guidelines are retained for historical reference but not actively enforced. Defaults to true.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the guideline was created. ISO 8601 format. Marks when the policy rule was first established in the system.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the guideline was last modified. ISO 8601 format. Updated when policy descriptions or enforcement rules change.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the guideline was soft-deleted or made inactive. ISO 8601 format. Null for active guidelines. Soft deletion preserves historical audit trail of policy changes and allows recovery.

IDiscussionBoardContentGuideline.description:
Content policy rules and moderation guidelines that define community standards for articles and comments.

The content guidelines entity stores the authoritative rules that moderators enforce when reviewing articles and monitoring comments. Each guideline entry specifies a policy rule, whether it applies to articles or comments, the severity level if violated, and examples to help moderators make consistent decisions.

Guidelines are organized by policy area (hate speech, misinformation, spam, off-topic, etc.) and include detailed descriptions of prohibited behavior. The system maintains the complete set of active guidelines for reference by moderators and contributors. Soft deletion is supported to preserve historical policy changes while maintaining audit trails of previous guidelines.

Moderation decisions reference specific guidelines when removing content or issuing warnings, creating accountability and transparency about why content was removed.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1. Used to navigate through paginated results.

limit.description: Number of queue items per page. Maximum 100 items. Defaults to 20 if not specified.

oneOf.description: Default priority for standard articles awaiting review.
Expedited review flag for urgent submissions or special circumstances.
Secondary priority for routine content review.

priority.description: Filter by priority level: 'normal' (default), 'high' (expedited review), 'low' (secondary priority). Optional. If specified, only queue items with this priority are returned.

assigned_moderator_id.description: Filter by assigned moderator UUID. Optional. If specified, returns only queue items assigned to this moderator. If null, returns unassigned items.

contributor_id.description: Filter by contributor UUID. Optional. If specified, returns only queue items submitted by this contributor.

submitted_date_from.description: Start of submission date range (ISO 8601 format). Optional. Returns queue items submitted on or after this date.

submitted_date_to.description: End of submission date range (ISO 8601 format). Optional. Returns queue items submitted on or before this date.

oneOf.description: Sort by submission timestamp (oldest first for standard FIFO workflow).
Sort by priority level (high priority first for urgent item management).

sort_by.description: Sort order for results: 'submitted_at' (oldest first, standard FIFO workflow), 'priority' (high priority first). Defaults to 'submitted_at' if not specified.

oneOf.description: Ascending order - oldest submissions first for submitted_at, lowest priority first for priority field.
Descending order - newest submissions first for submitted_at, highest priority first for priority field.

sort_order.description: Sort direction: 'asc' (ascending), 'desc' (descending). Defaults to 'asc' for submitted_at (oldest first) and 'desc' for priority (highest first).

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for the moderation queue with pagination and sorting options.

Enables moderators to efficiently navigate and manage the article review queue with flexible filtering capabilities. Supports filtering by priority level, submission date range, assigned moderator, and contributor author. Results can be sorted by submission timestamp for standard FIFO workflow or by priority for urgent item management.

All filter parameters are optional. When no filters are specified, returns all pending queue items in default order.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation queue entry. Generated as UUID v4 upon creation and persists for the lifetime of the queue record.

discussion_board_article_id.description: Reference to the article awaiting review. Links this queue entry to the specific article in the discussion_board_articles table that requires moderator approval.

discussion_board_contributor_id.description: Reference to the contributor who submitted the article. Links this queue entry to the submitting contributor in the discussion_board_contributors table, enabling moderators to assess contributor history and context when reviewing articles.

submitted_at.description: Timestamp when the article was submitted for review in ISO 8601 format. Used as the primary sort field for queue ordering in standard FIFO (first-in-first-out) workflow mode, ensuring older submissions are reviewed first by default.

priority.description: Priority level for moderator review workflow prioritization. Controls review urgency and queue sorting. Values: 'normal' (default priority for standard articles), 'high' (flagged for expedited review due to urgency or special circumstances), 'low' (secondary priority for routine content).

assigned_moderator_id.description: Reference to moderator assigned for review, if any. Contains UUID of the assigned moderator from discussion_board_moderators table. Null value indicates the queue item is unassigned and awaiting moderator pickup. Assignment enables workload distribution and progress tracking across the moderation team.

review_started_at.description: Timestamp when a moderator began reviewing the article in ISO 8601 format. Null indicates the queue item has not yet entered active review. This field tracks review lifecycle progression and enables identification of items in-progress versus unreviewed.

submission_notes.description: Optional notes from contributor explaining the article or addressing previous feedback. Maximum 1000 characters. Null if no notes provided. Helps moderators understand context and intent behind submitted content, particularly useful for articles addressing prior review comments.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the queue entry was created in ISO 8601 format. Represents when the article was added to the moderation queue. Used for audit trail purposes and administrative tracking of queue entry lifecycle.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this queue entry in ISO 8601 format. Tracks when any field of this queue record was modified, including assignment changes or review status updates. Essential for audit compliance and understanding recent activity on queue items.

IDiscussionBoardModerationQueue.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of moderation queue entries for list views and moderator dashboards.

Represents individual items in the article moderation queue, tracking articles submitted by contributors awaiting moderator approval, rejection, or revision requests. Each queue entry captures submission context, assignment status, and review progress.

The queue is the central workflow mechanism for the moderation system. When contributors submit articles, queue entries are created automatically to initiate the review process. Moderators retrieve queue items through this summary view to prioritize their workload, filter by urgency or contributor, and track which articles are unreviewed, in-progress, or ready for decision.

The summary variant provides essential information for efficient queue management including article reference, contributor reference, submission timestamp, priority level, moderator assignment, and review status. It excludes detailed audit trail data and full schema to optimize performance in list views where many queue entries may be displayed simultaneously.

Workflow Context: Queue items are created when articles reach pending_approval status. They persist until moderators approve or reject the article, at which point they remain in the queue table for audit purposes but are no longer actively retrieved by moderator workflows.

IDiscussionBoardContentViolationRecord.I.description:
Search and filtering parameters for content policy violation records.

This request DTO enables moderators to query violation records with powerful filtering capabilities across violation type, contributor, severity level, enforcement action, moderator, and date range. Used in paginated list operations that return violation history for pattern analysis, moderator performance review, and escalation decisions.

The violation records table maintains an immutable audit trail of all policy breaches detected in articles and comments. Moderators use filters to identify violation patterns (repeated offenses of specific types), review individual contributor violation history (complete enforcement context), focus on severe violations (priority review), verify enforcement consistency (by action type or moderator), analyze violations within time windows (trend analysis), and track moderator performance (who documented violations).

All filter fields are optional and combine additively to narrow results. Pagination parameters control result set size and position. Sorting options enable different analytical perspectives on violation data—temporal analysis (most recent first), severity-focused review (most severe first).

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not specified. Combined with limit to retrieve specific result set windows for large violation datasets.

limit.description: Number of violation records per page. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Maximum 100 records per page. Controls result set size for pagination.

oneOf.description: Violations targeting protected groups with hateful content or slurs.
Violations attacking individuals personally rather than addressing topic or argument.
Violations spreading false or misleading claims presented as fact.
Violations involving coordinated or repeated targeting of specific users.
Violations containing promotional content, solicitation, or repeated similar messages.
Violations posting content unrelated to discussion or article topic.
Violations displaying explicit violence, sexual content, or graphic imagery.
Violations containing threats of violence or serious harm to individuals or groups.
Violations involving copyright infringement or intellectual property violations.
Violations of other community policy types not covered by specific categories.

violation_type.description: Filter by specific violation type. Optional. When specified, returns only violations of this classification. Enables pattern analysis for specific violation categories (e.g., identifying repeated misinformation violations from specific contributors).

contributor_id.description: Filter by contributor ID to review complete violation history for a specific user. Optional. When specified, returns all violations recorded against this contributor, enabling assessment of individual behavior patterns, violation frequency, escalation trajectory, and enforcement history context for suspension/restriction decisions.

moderator_id.description: Filter by moderator ID to review violations documented by a specific moderator. Optional. When specified, returns all violation records created by this moderator, enabling moderation team performance analysis, consistency review, and quality assessment of violation documentation practices.

oneOf.description: Small issues that violate policy but are correctable through editing.
Clear policy violations requiring enforcement action and content removal.
Serious violations like hate speech or threats requiring immediate escalation.

severity_level.description: Filter by violation severity level. Optional. When specified, returns only violations classified at this severity. Enables focus on serious violations for priority moderation review and escalation assessment.

oneOf.description: Moderator edited content to comply with policy while preserving intent.
Violating content deleted from platform.
Warning issued to user about policy violation.
User posting restricted temporarily due to repeated violations.
User account suspended for serious or repeated violations.
Violation escalated to administrator for further investigation or action.

action_taken.description: Filter by enforcement action taken in response to violation. Optional. When specified, returns only violations where this specific action was taken. Enables verification of enforcement consistency across similar violations and review of action pattern appropriateness.

date_from.description: Filter violations detected on or after this ISO 8601 datetime. Optional. When combined with date_to, creates date range filter for temporal analysis of violation trends, seasonal patterns, or incident investigations.

date_to.description: Filter violations detected on or before this ISO 8601 datetime. Optional. When combined with date_from, creates date range for reviewing recent violations or historical enforcement patterns.

oneOf.description: Sort by when violation was detected. Defaults to this field if order_by not specified.
Sort by severity classification for severity-focused review priorities.

order_by.description: Field to sort results by. Defaults to 'detection_date' (most recent first) if not specified. Enables different analytical perspectives on violation data.

Descending order. Shows most recent violations first (for detection_date) or most severe first (for severity_level). Default direction.

order_direction.description: Sort direction for the selected order_by field. Defaults to 'desc' if not specified.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorAuditLog.IReque.description:
Search and filtering parameters for moderation audit log entries.

This request DTO enables moderators to query the immutable, append-only audit trail of all moderation actions performed on the platform. Supports advanced multi-dimensional filtering across action type, moderator, affected contributor, related content (articles/comments), date range, and reason text to enable compliance review, dispute investigation, moderation quality analysis, and regulatory audits.

The audit log maintains a complete record of every action performed by moderators—article approvals/rejections/edits/deletions/archiving/pinning/locking, comment edits/removals, user warnings/restrictions/suspensions/unsuspensions—ensuring full visibility into moderation decisions, reasoning, and enforcement patterns. All filter fields are optional and combine to narrow results for targeted audit examination.

The audit log is read-only from the API perspective (entries created only through moderation actions), ensuring immutability and integrity of the compliance record. Entries are never modified or deleted after creation, preserving authoritative history for appeals, regulatory compliance, and institutional accountability.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not specified. Used with limit to retrieve specific result set windows from potentially thousands of audit log entries.

limit.description: Number of audit log entries per page. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Maximum 100 entries per page. Controls result set size for pagination of audit records.

Moderator rejected article from publication.
Moderator edited article content to comply with policy.
Moderator removed article from platform.
Moderator archived article to remove from active listings.
Moderator pinned article to featured position.
Moderator unpinned article from featured position.
Moderator locked article to prevent new comments.
Moderator unlocked article to allow new comments.
Moderator edited comment content to comply with policy.
Moderator removed comment from platform.
Moderator issued warning to user about policy violation.
Moderator applied posting restrictions to user account.
Moderator suspended user account.
Moderator lifted suspension from user account.
Moderator created violation record documenting policy breach.

moderator_id.description: Filter by moderator ID to review actions performed by a specific moderator. Optional. When specified, returns all audit entries where this moderator was the actor, enabling performance review, consistency analysis of individual moderator decisions, and quality assessment of moderation patterns.

affected_contributor_id.description: Filter by affected contributor ID to review all moderation actions taken against a specific user. Optional. When specified, returns all audit entries where this contributor was the subject of the action, showing complete enforcement history for dispute investigation, appeals, or escalation review.

article_id.description: Filter by article ID to review all moderation actions related to a specific article. Optional. When specified, returns audit entries for actions taken on this article (approval, rejection, deletion, archiving, pinning, locking), enabling investigation of specific content moderation decisions and timeline.

comment_id.description: Filter by comment ID to review all moderation actions taken on a specific comment. Optional. When specified, returns audit entries for actions taken on this comment (editing, removal, user warnings related to comment), enabling review of individual comment moderation decisions.

date_to.description: Filter audit log entries created on or before this ISO 8601 datetime. Optional. When combined with date_from, creates date range for reviewing recent moderation activity or historical audit trails for specific periods.

reason_search.description: Full-text search across moderator-provided reason/justification text in audit log entries. Optional. When specified, returns entries where the reason field contains this text, enabling text-based search of moderator reasoning, justification, and decision documentation.

oneOf.description: Sort by when action was performed. Defaults to this field if order_by not specified.
Sort by action type for action-focused analysis.
Sort by moderator for moderator performance analysis.

oneOf.description: Ascending order. Shows oldest entries first (for created_at) or earlier action types first.
Descending order. Shows most recent entries first (for created_at). Default direction.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.description:
Suspension and restriction record for a contributor account.

Represents an enforcement action taken against a contributor who has violated community guidelines. Each suspension captures the violation context, enforcement type, duration, and resolution status. Suspensions are immutable after creation; only status transitions can be recorded via updates.

Suspensions track contributor restrictions including posting limitations, account lockouts, and permanent bans. The record maintains the complete lifecycle from initial suspension through expiration or manual lifting, enabling moderators to review enforcement history and contributors to understand their account status. Suspension records are retained indefinitely for compliance and pattern analysis.

Used in moderation operations for recording enforcement actions, reviewing contributor account restrictions, and enforcing escalation policies based on violation patterns.

id.description: Unique identifier for this suspension record. Generated as UUID v4 by the system on creation.

contributor.description: The contributor whose account is suspended. Provides context about the restricted user including their identification and display name.

moderator.description: The moderator who issued this suspension. Identifies the enforcement authority and accountability for the suspension decision.

suspension_type.description:
Type of suspension enforcement determining which actions are restricted.

- posting_restriction: Contributor cannot create articles or post comments while retaining login access
- account_suspension: Contributor cannot login or access any board features
- permanent_ban: Account is permanently disabled with no expiration or recovery option

Each type represents escalating enforcement severity and operational restrictions.

reason.description: Detailed explanation for the suspension action. Documents the specific policy violations and context that led to this enforcement decision. Maximum 1000 characters. Used for transparency to the contributor and for moderator records.

severity_level.description:
Severity classification of the violation determining escalation track and enforcement messaging.

- minor: First offense with proportional light restriction
- moderate: Repeated minor violations or single moderate violation
- severe: Repeated violations or serious single violation requiring suspension
- permanent: Irreversible ban for severe violations or repeated severe violations

Severity classification guides both the enforcement approach and contributor messaging.

duration_days.description: Duration of suspension in days for time-limited suspensions. Null for permanent suspensions. Used to calculate automatic expiration timestamp. Typical values: 3 (minor), 7 (moderate), 30 (severe). System automatically lifts restrictions when duration expires.

suspended_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension became effective and restrictions were applied to the contributor account.

expiration_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension expires and account restrictions are automatically lifted. Null for permanent suspensions with no expiration. System uses this to determine active suspension status.

status.description:
Current status of the suspension determining whether restrictions apply.

- active: Restrictions are currently in effect and enforced
- lifted: Moderator manually removed the suspension before expiration
- expired: Suspension duration completed naturally and restrictions automatically removed

Status field controls enforcement logic and visibility of suspension to the contributor.

lifted_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension was manually lifted by a moderator. Null if suspension has not been lifted or expired naturally. Used to track early removal decisions.

lift_reason.description: Explanation for why the suspension was lifted. Documents the moderator's decision to remove restrictions before natural expiration. Maximum 500 characters. Null if suspension not yet lifted. Used for accountability and future reference.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension record was created. Indicates when the enforcement action was recorded and became effective.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the suspension record. Changes when status, lift_reason, or other fields are modified. Used to track record history.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying suspension records.

Supports comprehensive filtering across suspension dimensions including affected contributor, imposing moderator, suspension type, severity level, and date ranges. Full-text search enables finding suspensions by contributor name or suspension reason.

Results are paginated and sortable. Default sorting is by suspended_at descending (most recent first) to show active suspensions prominently. Alternative sorting options enable analysis by expiration date, severity, contributor, or moderator for different moderation workflows.

Used to retrieve suspension lists with advanced search and filtering capabilities for moderators to track restrictions, review enforcement history, and analyze policy compliance patterns.

id.description: Unique identifier for the account restriction record.

oneOf.description: Restriction type enforced. Prevents contributors from posting articles and comments while allowing login.
Restriction type enforced. Prevents contributor login and account access for the specified duration.
Restriction type enforced. Permanently disables the contributor account with no expiration.

restriction_type.description:
Type of restriction applied. Determines enforcement mechanism and access level restrictions.

Valid restriction types:
- posting_restriction: Contributor cannot create articles or post comments
- temporary_suspension: Account login denied for specified duration
- permanent_ban: Account permanently disabled

Restriction type determines which contributor actions are blocked during the active period.

imposed_at.description: Timestamp when the restriction was applied in ISO 8601 format. Marks the enforcement action time.

expires_at.description: Timestamp when the restriction automatically expires. Null for permanent bans or indefinite restrictions. After this timestamp, restriction is no longer enforced and account returns to normal operation.

lifted_at.description: Timestamp when the restriction was manually lifted by a moderator. Null if restriction expired naturally or is still active. Enables early restriction removal for rehabilitated contributors.

imposed_by_moderator.description: The moderator who imposed the restriction. Identifies the enforcement authority.

- active: Restrictions currently in effect
- lifted: Moderator manually removed the restriction
- expired: Restriction duration completed naturally

IDiscussionBoardAccountRestriction.description:
Account restriction record representing enforcement actions taken against contributor accounts.

Account restrictions and suspensions are imposed by moderators to enforce community standards. Restrictions prevent contributors from creating articles or posting comments during the restriction period. Multiple restriction types are supported: posting restrictions (3-day, 7-day, custom), temporary suspensions (7-day, 30-day), and permanent bans.

Each restriction records the restriction type, reason, start timestamp, end timestamp (null for active indefinite bans), and moderator who imposed it. Restrictions can be manually lifted by moderators before the scheduled end date. Complete restriction history is retained for compliance and pattern analysis.

Active restrictions (where current time is before end_date or end_date is null) prevent new article submissions and comment posts. Multiple overlapping restrictions are not allowed; applying a new restriction cancels any previous restriction.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Controls how many restriction records are returned in each response.

moderator_id.description: Filter by the imposing moderator. Returns restrictions imposed by this specific moderator.

Permanently disables the contributor account with no expiration.

restriction_type.description: Filter by restriction type. Narrows results to restrictions of the specified enforcement category, enabling analysis by enforcement mechanism.

oneOf.description: Restrictions currently in effect and being enforced.
Restrictions manually removed by moderator before scheduled expiration.
Restrictions whose duration completed naturally without manual intervention.

status.description: Filter by restriction status. Distinguishes between active enforcement, manual lifting, and natural expiration to support different moderation workflows.

imposed_from.description: Filter by restriction imposition date (inclusive). Returns restrictions imposed on or after this timestamp.

imposed_to.description: Filter by restriction imposition date (inclusive). Returns restrictions imposed on or before this timestamp.

expires_from.description: Filter by expiration date (inclusive). Returns restrictions expiring on or after this timestamp.

expires_to.description: Filter by expiration date (inclusive). Returns restrictions expiring on or before this timestamp.

Descending order from latest to earliest or Z to A.

order.description: Sort order direction. Controls whether results are ordered in ascending or descending sequence.

IDiscussionBoardAccountRestriction.IRequ.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for querying account restriction records.

Supports comprehensive filtering across restriction dimensions including restricted contributor, imposing moderator, restriction type, and date ranges. Full-text search enables finding restrictions by contributor name or restriction reason.

Results are paginated and sortable. Default sorting is by imposed_at descending (most recent restrictions first) to show active enforcement actions. Alternative sorting options enable analysis by expiration date, restriction type, contributor, or moderator for different moderation workflows.

Used to retrieve restriction lists with advanced search and filtering capabilities for moderators to review enforcement actions, track active restrictions, and analyze compliance patterns.

oneOf.description: Contributor cannot create articles or post comments but retains login access.
Contributor cannot login to the account or access any features.
Account is permanently disabled with no expiration or recovery option.

suspension_type.description: Type of suspension to enforce. Required. Determines which actions are restricted for the contributor during the suspension period. Each type represents an escalating enforcement level from posting restrictions to complete account disabling.

reason.description: Detailed explanation for the suspension action. Required. Maximum 1000 characters. Must document the specific policy violations, escalation events, or circumstances that led to this suspension decision. Used for transparency and future reference.

oneOf.description: First offense with light restriction. Used for initial violations with minor consequences.
Second offense with extended restriction. Applied after repeated minor violations or moderate violations.
Repeated violations or serious single violation. Applied for habitual violators or severe conduct violations.
Irreversible account ban for the most severe violations or repeated severe violations.

severity_level.description: Severity classification of the violation. Required. Determines escalation track and enforcement messaging. Severity classification drives both the enforcement type applied and the messaging provided to the contributor regarding their account status.

duration_days.description: Duration of suspension in days for time-limited suspensions. Optional. Typical values: 3 (minor escalation), 7 (moderate escalation), 30 (severe escalation). Custom durations allowed. Used to calculate automatic expiration timestamp. Must be 0 or positive if provided. Omit or use null for permanent suspensions with no expiration.

IDiscussionBoardUserSuspension.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new account suspension or posting restriction.

Captures the disciplinary action details moderators must specify when suspending or restricting a contributor account for policy violations. The moderator ID is automatically populated from authentication context; the contributor ID comes from the URL path parameter. The suspended_at timestamp is set to current time, and status is initialized to 'active'.

For time-limited suspensions, duration_days is used to calculate expiration_at. For permanent suspensions, duration_days is omitted or null, and expiration_at is set to null. The suspension becomes immediately effective upon creation.

Suspension records are immutable after creation; only status transitions (active → lifted) are allowed via separate update operations with lift_reason documentation.

IDiscussionBoardAccountRestriction.ICrea.description:
Request body for creating a new account restriction as a moderation enforcement action.

Captures the restriction details and enforcement parameters needed to impose a posting restriction, temporary suspension, or permanent ban on a contributor account. The moderator imposing the restriction (from authentication context) and timestamps are set by the system; only the restriction type, expiration date (if applicable), and enforcement reason are provided by the moderator.

The restriction_type field determines the enforcement mechanism and expected expiration behavior. For posting_restriction and temporary_suspension types, an expires_at timestamp is required to specify when the restriction expires. For permanent_ban type, expires_at should be null (or omitted) to indicate no automatic expiration. The reason field must explain the conduct that triggered this enforcement action and communicate the violation to the contributor.

discussion_board_contributor_id.description: Unique identifier of the contributor account to restrict. This must be a valid UUID of an existing contributor in the system.

oneOf.description: Type of restriction to apply. Valid values: 'posting_restriction' (prevent article/comment creation), 'temporary_suspension' (prevent login), 'permanent_ban' (permanently disable account). This determines the enforcement mechanism and expected duration behavior.

restriction_type.description: Type of restriction to apply. Valid values: 'posting_restriction' (prevent article/comment creation), 'temporary_suspension' (prevent login), 'permanent_ban' (permanently disable account). This determines the enforcement mechanism and expected duration behavior.

reason.description: Explanation of why the restriction is being imposed. Must describe the conduct that violated community guidelines and explain the enforcement decision to the contributor. Required field, 1-500 characters.

oneOf.description: Timestamp in ISO 8601 format when this restriction should automatically expire and no longer be enforced. Required for posting_restriction and temporary_suspension types.
Use null for permanent_ban type to indicate no automatic expiration.

expires_at.description: Timestamp in ISO 8601 format when this temporary restriction automatically expires. Required for posting_restriction and temporary_suspension types; should be null for permanent_ban type. Determines when the contributor's account returns to normal operation.

lifted_reason.description: Reason for manually lifting the restriction. Documents the moderator's decision and communicates the explanation to the contributor. Maximum 500 characters. Required when lifting a restriction.

IDiscussionBoardAccountRestriction.IUpda.description:
Request body for lifting an active account restriction.

When a moderator determines that a previously-restricted contributor has demonstrated rehabilitation or the restriction was applied in error, they can use this operation to restore the account to normal operation immediately. The operation updates the restriction record with the lift timestamp and the moderator who performed the action. A reason for lifting is required, which documents the decision and communicates the explanation to the contributor.

id.description: Unique identifier for the article category. Generated as UUID v4 on creation.

code.description: Unique machine-readable identifier for the category (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance'). Used for API references, internal routing, and category selection. Must be 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens.

name.description: Human-readable display name for the category shown in user interfaces. Examples include 'Economic Policy' and 'Political Governance'. Used in category selection dropdowns, article listings, and navigation menus. Must be 10-100 characters.

display_order.description: Numeric sort order for displaying categories in user interfaces. Lower numbers appear first in category menus and navigation. Controls the sequence of category options presented to users. Defaults to 0.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this category is currently available for article submission. Active categories appear in category selection when users create articles. Inactive categories persist for historical reference but prevent new articles from being assigned. Defaults to true.

article_count.description: Denormalized count of published articles currently assigned to this category. Used for display purposes (e.g., 'Economic Policy (47 articles)'). Updated automatically when articles are published or unpublished. Should be recalculated periodically for accuracy. Defaults to 0.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary.description:
Lightweight category summary for efficient display in selection interfaces and category reference contexts.

Provides essential category information needed for article categorization and user-facing category menus. Includes unique identifier, machine-readable code, display name, sort order, active status, and article count for quick reference without additional lookups.

This summary variant is optimized for list operations where multiple categories are displayed simultaneously. It excludes detailed description content and timestamp information to minimize payload size and improve API response performance.

Used in category selection dropdowns when creating articles, category listing views for browsing, and embedded references within article summary representations where full category details are not required.

id.description: Unique identifier for the content guideline policy rule. Generated as UUID v4 when the guideline is created.

code.description: Machine-readable identifier for the guideline policy (e.g., 'hate-speech', 'misinformation', 'spam', 'off-topic'). Used in moderation logs, audit trails, and violation records to create a consistent policy reference. Must be 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens.

title.description: Short, descriptive title of the policy guideline displayed in moderation dashboards, violation notices, and contributor warnings. Examples include 'Hate Speech', 'Misinformation', and 'Commercial Spam'. Must be 10-100 characters.

oneOf.description: Minor violation severity. Typical consequences include content editing, contributor warning, or educational feedback. Used for borderline violations or first-time policy breaches.
Moderate violation severity. Typical consequences include content removal, warning to contributor, or temporary posting restrictions. Used for clear policy violations without severe impact.
Severe violation severity. Typical consequences include content removal, account suspension, or permanent removal for repeated violations. Used for serious policy breaches or harmful content.

severity_level.description: Classification of violation severity that guides moderator response proportionality. Informs escalation decisions and enforcement consistency across the platform. Different severity levels trigger different enforcement actions.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this guideline is currently being enforced by moderators. Active guidelines are displayed in policy documentation and referenced during content moderation. Inactive guidelines are retained for historical reference but not actively applied to new content. Defaults to true.

IDiscussionBoardContentGuideline.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary representation of content guidelines for moderation dashboard and policy reference contexts.

Provides essential policy information that moderators need to quickly identify and reference content policies when reviewing articles and comments. Includes policy code, title, and severity classification to support rapid decision-making in moderation workflows without requiring full policy documentation.

This summary variant is optimized for list operations and dashboard displays where many guidelines may be shown simultaneously. It excludes detailed policy descriptions, examples, applicability scope, and violation consequences to minimize payload size while retaining the core information needed for moderation reference.

Used in moderation violation lists to show which policy was breached, policy selection when creating violations, and dashboard displays for moderator training and reference. Full guideline details with examples and rationale available via main IDiscussionBoardContentGuideline type.

id.description: Unique identifier for the violation record. Generated automatically as UUID upon record creation.

violation_type.description: Specific type of policy violation detected in the content. Possible values: 'hate_speech' (targeting protected groups), 'personal_attack' (attacking individuals), 'misinformation' (false claims), 'harassment' (coordinated targeting), 'spam' (promotional content), 'off_topic' (unrelated content), 'graphic_content' (explicit imagery/violence), 'threats' (violence or harm threats), 'copyright' (copyright violations), or 'other' (miscellaneous violations).

severity.description: Severity classification of the violation determining enforcement response. Classification: 'minor' (small correctable issues), 'moderate' (clear policy violation requiring action), or 'severe' (serious violations like hate speech or threats requiring immediate escalation).

violation_description.description: Detailed description of what was violated and why it violates community policy. Includes specific examples from the content that triggered the violation. Maximum 2000 characters, providing context for understanding the violation determination.

action_taken.description: Enforcement action taken by the moderator in response to the violation. Possible actions: 'edited' (moderator corrected the content), 'removed' (content deleted), 'warned' (user warned), 'restricted' (posting restrictions applied), 'suspended' (account suspended), or 'reported_to_admin' (escalated to administrator). Documents the moderation response.

detected_at.description: Timestamp when the violation was detected by the moderator or automated system. Records the exact moment of violation discovery.

contributor.description: Summary identification of the contributor who created the violating content. Provides contributor context for understanding violation patterns and contributor history.

moderator.description: Summary identification of the moderator who documented and recorded this violation. Tracks moderation accountability and decision-making.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the violation record was created in the system. Establishes authoritative record of when the violation was officially documented.

IDiscussionBoardContentViolationRecord.I.description:
Summary view of a content violation record optimized for list displays and audit logging.

Provides essential information about a policy violation including the specific violation type, severity level, action taken, and the violating content description. Includes identification of both the contributing user who created the violating content and the moderator who recorded the violation.

Omits optional contextual fields (action_details, content_snapshot) to optimize list view performance while retaining critical enforcement information.

Used in moderation dashboards, violation history lists, and compliance audit trails to track enforcement actions and contributor violation patterns.

id.description: Unique identifier for the audit log entry. Generated automatically as UUID upon action logging.

action_type.description: Type of moderator action performed. Possible values: 'article_approved' (article approved for publication), 'article_rejected' (article rejected from publication), 'article_edited' (moderator edited article), 'article_deleted' (article removed), 'article_archived' (article archived), 'article_pinned' (article featured at top), 'article_unpinned' (featured status removed), 'article_locked' (comments disabled), 'article_unlocked' (comments enabled), 'comment_edited' (comment edited), 'comment_removed' (comment deleted), 'user_warned' (warning issued), 'user_restricted' (posting restricted), 'user_suspended' (account suspended), 'user_unsuspended' (suspension lifted), or 'violation_recorded' (violation documented). Documents the specific action taken.

oneOf.description: Explanation of why the action was taken. For rejections, the reason for rejection. For removals, the guideline violated. For restrictions, the reason for restriction. For approvals, optional notes. Maximum 1000 characters.
Null if no explanation was provided for the action.

reason.description: Optional explanation of why the action was taken. Provides context for moderation decisions enabling audit trail clarity and appeal handling.

moderator.description: Summary identification of the moderator who performed the action. Tracks who made moderation decisions for accountability and performance analysis.

affected_contributor.description: Summary identification of the contributor affected by the action. Present when the action directly impacts a user (warnings, restrictions, suspensions). Null for content-only actions like article approval. Tracks which contributors are subject to enforcement actions.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the action was performed. This is the authoritative timestamp for when the moderation action occurred in the system.

IDiscussionBoardModeratorAuditLog.ISumma.description:
Summary view of a moderator audit log entry optimized for list displays and compliance review.

Provides essential information about a moderation action including the action type, the moderator who performed it, the affected contributor (if applicable), and the action timestamp. Includes an optional reason field explaining the moderation decision.

Omits detailed state transition information (old_status, new_status) and extensive metadata to optimize list view performance while preserving critical accountability information.

Used in moderation audit trails, moderator activity dashboards, compliance reviews, and appeal handling to track all moderation decisions and enforce accountability standards.
